The Sycamore Creek near Dugas stream gauge (SNDA3) measured a rapid 4 foot rise. Flow was approximately 1000 CFS.
The USGS stream gage on Granite Creek in Prescott (GCRA3) reported a 2.9 ft rise in 45 minutes from multiple rounds of heavy rainfall upstream during the afternoon.

Slow moving thunderstorms produced torrential rain over southeastern Val Verde County near the Del Rio area early on July 16. Radar estimates indicated 3 to 11 inches of rain in southeastern Val Verde County with the heaviest amounts falling in rural portions of the county. CoCoRaHS observers recorded 4 to 6 inches of rain in Del Rio and the Del Rio International Airport recorded 4.72 inches of rain. San Felipe Creek swelled beyond its banks, reaching a crest of 16.99ft (6,010cfs) at 1000CST.||Flash flooding was reported by broadcast media in multiple locations in Del Rio, impacting…
Thunderstorms produced locally heavy rain that led to flash flooding closing numerous roads in Bandera County.

Thunderstorms produced locally heavy rain that led to flash flooding near Bandera Falls. There was significant flooding over FM 1283 near Red Bluff Creek. Water topped the bridge over the creek and swept away the bridge's guardrails.

Numerous roads were closed near Leakey and Rio Frio due to flooding caused by heavy rain along the Frio and Dry Frio rivers. Multiple river crossings were flooded. Portions of RR1120 saw around 9 ft of inundation. Inundation reached the grounds of an RV park in Rio Frio but did not cause significant damage.

Numerous county roads were flooded and closed across Medina County following heavy rainfall. US90 became impassable between Hondo and Uvalde in both directions. TX173 became impassable along Middle Verde Creek. At least 4 high water rescues occurred across the county before 0700CST, including at least two rescues involving motorists swept off in low water crossings.
Reports of flooded roadways near Bradford Regional Airport.
High water covered Shreve Park Drive near Technology Drive off of Highway 3132. Report from mPING.
A water rescue was needed for a vehicle stuck in high water in a typical flood prone area.

Numerous reports of flash flooding were received from the north side of Tyrone. Roads impacted include West 20th Street, Hamlin and Lincoln avenues. Water was reported to be 2.5 feet deep in some spots, restricting access to emergency responders.
Flash flooding pushed water up to the bottom of the first floor of the paper mill and Pennsylvania Ave was completely underwater.
There was water flowing behind Tates Creek Mini Mart and onto the road.
Water was flowing over East Hickman Road at the intersection with Tates Creek Road.
There were multiple vehicles stalled in water near the intersections of 7th Street and West Magnolia Avenue and 7th Street and Davies Street.
Water was over the 800 block of Red Cross Road. Black top was missing from the roadway.
A USFS engine crew reported rocks and debris on State Route 89 due to flash flooding. Time is estimated.

The Batesville area was impacted by flooding along the Leona River triggered by heavy rain concentrated in Uvalde County north of Batesville. Initial rises on the Leona River on July 16 flooded portions of US57 near Batesville. A much more significant rise occurred in the early morning of July 17, when floodwaters along the Leona River reached the community between 0000 and 0200CST, causing widespread flooding.||Inundation spread across much of the eastern half of Batesville and extended to FM117, impacting many residences east and some west of the highway. The greatest inundation extent was…

Thunderstorms produced locally heavy rain that led to flash flooding near Bandera Falls. English Crossing Rd. was flooded at the Medina River. A picture showed the Medina River sign on the side of the road nearly underwater.

Thunderstorms produced locally heavy rain that led to flash flooding in Ingram. There were several water rescues and multiple roads flooded and impassable including the intersection of Candlelite Dr. and Skyview Dr.

Public reports and radar estimates indicated around 8 to 12 inches of rain fell in the D'Hanis area on the morning of July 14. Widespread flooding occurred in D'Hanis due to a combination of riverine flooding along Seco and Parker creeks and poor drainage following torrential rains. All roads in D'Hanis south of US90 had standing water and water was observed surrounding homes and businesses. However, no structures sustained floodwater inundation. The CR429 crossing over Seco Creek was flooded.

Several roadways were flooded in the Concan and Reagan Wells area from July 14 through July 16. Roads around Garner State Park were closed. RR1051 in Reagan Wells saw at least 2ft of inundation. Crossings across the Frio River between 7 Bluffs Crossing and Kenneth Arthur Crossing were flooded. The Frio River overtopped the FM1050 bridge at Garner State Park and over TX127. Rises on the Dry Frio River overtopped six river crossings in Reagan Wells, causing some washouts. Several residences were flooded and residents were stranded for up to a week due to the flooded crossings.
A flooded basement was reported in Rixford.
Water was flowing over the roadway near the intersection of Wallace Avenue and John Hill Taylor Drive in Leitchfield.
Two children were rescued from flood waters and treated for injuries near the paper mill in Tyrone. Both children were treated for injuries.
properties.epi: A stationary front stationed across central Pennsylvania allowed for a lifting mechanism for showers and storms during the morning and afternoon hours of July 5, 2026. Showers and isolated thunderstorms began to develop across portions of western and central Pennsylvaia during the late morning hours and began to exhibit slow forward motion and instances of training. This continued into the afternoon and evening hours, where heavy rainfall persisted over Tyrone in Blair County for upwards of an hour. This prompted considerable flash flooding in the borough, with multiple homes being flooded and some roadways taking on between two and three feet of water. There were also two children that were rescued from flood waters near the paper mill in Tyrone due to the flooding. Given the unstable airmass, thunderstorms continued to grow upscale throughout the afternoon and evening hours,…

properties.note: Water was observed across several roads, including near the junction of 303rd Ave and 218th St, and parts of Highway 1806 in southeast Stanley County. Water was also forced out of its banks along LaRoche Creek.

Moccasin Creek entered flood early in the morning of July 8th, after heavy rainfall in the city of Aberdeen, and remained in flood through mid-morning. The creek crested 6.51 feet, or 0.51 feet above flood stage.
An office for people with developmental disabilities in Valatie was evacuated due to flooding with 6 residents needing to be relocated.
An office for people with developmental disabilities in Valatie was evacuated due to flooding with 6 residents needing to be relocated.
Hollowville Community Mobile Park in Claverack evacuated due to flooding.
Hollowville Community Mobile Park in Claverack evacuated due to flooding.
Lexington Road near Cornell Place was closed due to flooding.
Water was across US Highway 62 West.
The area under the railroad overpass on North Mulberry was completely impassible and has several feet of standing water.
Several feet of water flooded the 5800 block of Priceville Road.
The stream gauge on Havasu Creek at the confluence with the Colorado River reported a rapid rise of 2.5 feet. The peak flow was 628 cfs.
A Facebook post from Navajo Nation Police reported flooding along Blue Canyon Road in Fort Defiance.
A Facebook post from Navajo Nation Police reported flooding along Navajo Route 54 in Fort Defiance.
A Facebook post from Navajo Nation Police reported flooding along Route 12 at Milepost 28.

The Chinle Creek at Chinle (CHCA3) stream gauge reported a 1. 7 foot rise, with a peak flow of 933 cfs. The creek rose into minor flood stage between 9:00 PM and 9:30 PM MST. A secondary rise into minor flood stage occurred between 11 PM and 11:30 PM MST. Peak discharge with the secondary rise was 781 cfs.
Water was reported flowing across county roads in southeastern Stanton County due to excessive rainfall from a very slow-moving thunderstorm.

Heavy rain in the headwaters of the Devils and Dry Devils River and associated draws led to extensive downstream rises with accompanying lowland flooding. The Devils River gages at Cauthorn Ranch near Juno and Bakers Crossing near Juno rose to 22.57 ft and 21.19 ft early on July 18, both in Major flood stage.||Empty kayaks were observed floating down the Devils River. The Devils River overtopped Highway 163 and rendered it impassable with several feet of water over the roadway. Flooding also occurred along the Devils River near Dolan Creek.
Thunderstorms produced locally heavy rain that led to flash flooding west of Ingram. Hwy 39 was fully closed between Ingram and Hwy 83 along the Guadalupe and South Fork Guadalupe Rivers.
Thunderstorms produced locally heavy rain that led to flash flooding in Ingram. Water rescues were with multiple streets flooded.

Heavy rain flooded streets in Sabinal beginning early on July 14, including Center St. At least two water rescues were reported in the area on July 14. A second round of heavy rain early on July 15 resulted in additional water rescues. US87 was flooded in spots between Sabinal and Utopia. TX127, RR187, and CR301 also experienced flooding. On July 16, the Sabinal River overtopped the TX127 bridge northwest of Sabinal. Around 2 ft of inundation was observed atop the RM1050 bridge over the Sabinal River in Utopia.

Around 1 ft of water was observed over US90 around 2 miles east of Knippa early on July 14 resulting in impassable conditions and closure of the highway. Widespread inundation was observed in surrounding areas near Dinner Creek. The flooding ultimately washed out portions of US90 at Dinner Creek near CR304. Portions of the railroad along US90 necessitated repairs after some track ballast was washed out. Several other roads in the Knippa area took on water, including FM1049 in several locations and other county roads and farm-to-market roads. Additional heavy rain on July 15 and July 16…
One foot of water was covering Hill Street and Main Street in Coalport. Cars reportedly stranded.
The public reported high water rushing into area streets in Osage.
Water was reported to be flowing across a stretch of old Route 22 in Walker Township.
Numerous cars reported to be underwater in Hummelstown near Swatara Creek. Reports of 3.5 to 4.0 inches of rain in only 45 minutes. Water rescues in progress.

Multiple flash flooding reports were received from locations in Glasgow, mainly from videos on social media. The majority of the reports included along Highway 2 near the Valley Event Center, the 6th Street underpass, the movie theater (Valley Cinemas) and near Reynolds Market. One to two foot depths on these roads were common. The rainfall was so intense that the water pumps in the underpass could not keep up. The water depth at the underpass was about 8 feet (estimated).

The Big Sioux River near Castlewood went into flood on the afternoon of July 9th as a result of multiple rounds of thunderstorms that delivered heavy rainfall across the southern Sisseton hills region on the evening of July 7th into the morning hours July 8th. The river crested at 9.26 feet, or 0.26 feet above flood stage during the early morning hours of July 10th and fell below flood later that morning. This level resulted in water over the culvert on 184th Street and the flooding of agricultural lands north of the town of Castlewood.
NY DOT reports flooding on NY 385 between Kings Road and the Rail Road Overpass in Coxsackie.
The 80 block of Iberia Road near the intersection of Peonia Road was flooded. When water receded rocks were left on the road.
Water covered the bridge over Cedar Creek, near the 9300 block of Kentucky Highway 643.

Around 3 to 4 inches of rain fell in eastern Freeborn county during the afternoon on Wednesday, July 8th. The Minnesota Department of Transportation reported that the heavy rainfall rates resulted in washed out roads that needed to be repaired the following day.

Ongoing flooding was reported along Swift Creek in the Many Glacier area. Flooding kept decreasing throughout the day, only with minor flooding to campgrounds and trails reported by the late morning hours on the 1st. Park rangers still reported continued water over hiking trails along with areas of low lying flooding on the 2nd.

The Moenkopi gauge (MOEA3) starting rising at 12:15 AM MST, rising 6.45 feet in 30 minutes. The water continued to rise to 32.66 feet at around 7:00 AM which is major flood stage, peaking at an estimated 9730 cfs. The gauge was knocked out of service at that time and didn't start recording again until early morning July 23rd. At that time the wash had gone back down to base flow.
The stream gauge on Phantom Creek (PHCA3) recorded a 2.6 ft rise.
The stream gauge on Bright Angel Creek near Phantom Ranch (BAPA3) recorded a 2 ft rise.
The stream gauge on Chinle Creek near Chinle (CHCA3) recorded a rapid 2.2 foot rise. Peak flow was shown to be 3358 cfs.
The stream gauge on Carrizo Creek near Show Low (CRZA3) recorded a 3.64 ft rise. Peak flow was 1255 cfs.
Reported numerous roads in town flooded with high water.
Thunderstorms produced locally heavy rain that led to flash flooding in Hunt. There were multiple water rescues in the town.
Thunderstorms produced locally heavy rain that led to flash flooding in Kerrville. Town Creek was in flood closing multiple streets. Floodwaters reached some homes.
Chest Creek is out of its banks. East Bridge Street and numerous smaller streets in Westover are already under one foot of water and the water is rising.

Heavy rainfall across portions of southeast Minnesota and northeast Iowa resulted in increased runoff into the Cedar River Basin. Consequently, downstream flow resulted in the Cedar River at Charles City to rise into flood stage during the afternoon on July 9th. The river crested in moderate flood stage at 17.54 feet before falling below flood stage during the morning on July 11th.

Heavy rainfall across portions of southeast Minnesota and northeast Iowa resulted in increased runoff into the Cedar River Basin. Consequently, downstream flow resulted in the Little Cedar River at Nashua to rise into flood stage during the morning on July 10th. The river crested in moderate flood stage before falling below flood stage during the afternoon on July 12th.

Heavy rainfall across portions of southeast Minnesota and northeast Iowa resulted in increased runoff into the Cedar River Basin. Consequently, downstream flow resulted in the Little Cedar River at Ionia to rise into flood stage during the late evening on July 10th. The river crested in moderate flood stage before falling below flood stage during the morning on July 12th.
Water rescue reported near Hart Avenue and Audubon Parkway. Additional water rescues were also reported around Louisville metro.
Flooded underpass beneath a railroad crossing in Hummelstown.
Water rescues underway on Hersheypark Drive near the Giant Center.
Two reports of flooded basements in Kane.
Several roads are flooded, and numerous homes have flooded basements.
VDOT reported standing water on I-95 near mile marker 68.2 in Chesterfield County. This led to the closure of the northbound left shoulder and left lane.

The Big Sioux River near Estelline rose above flood stage the evening of July 8th, cresting around 1.03 feet above flood stage (1645.03 feet) on July 9th. The river then fell below flood stage on the morning of July 11th.

The Big Sioux River near Bruce rose above flood stage during the early morning of July 10th, cresting around 0.47 feet above flood stage (8.47 feet) on July 1th. The river then fell below flood stage during the early morning of July 12th.
Trained spotter reported a local creek was flooded, with ponding and water running over the road crossing.

Willow Creek near Watertown went into flood on the afternoon of July 8th after a bout of heavy rainfall from multiple storms during the evening of July 7th and earlier that morning. The creek crested at 10.66 feet, 0.66 feet above flood stage, though with little to no impact before dropping out of flood later that evening.

Day County Emergency Management requested a local area emergency to limit travel due to heavy rainfall across the county, with reported flooding closing Highways 27 and 33 north of US-12. Rainfall from the CoCoRaHS observer near Roslyn topped out at 6.65 inches.
The Little Minnesota River near Peever went into flood during the morning hours of July 31st, but only stayed in flood for an hour and a half, cresting at 17.06 or 0.06 feet above flood stage.
A car was stuck in water near the 200 block of Siloam Road. There was approximately 10 inches of water on the roadway.
The stream gauge on the Agua Fria River at Cordes Lake (AFMA3) recorded a rapid 5 foot rise. Peak flow was 2780 cfs.
The stream gauge on Havasu Creek at the Colorado River (HNSA3) recorded a rapid 2.5 ft rise. The peak flow was 628 cfs.
Law Enforcement reported that a bridge is impassable near the corrections center in Supai.
Public sent video of a large flash flood on House Rock Wash at US 89A. Water was up to the bottom of the bridge.
Navajo Nation Parks and Recreation shared photos of swiftly flowing water in Antelope Creek. The tour area was evacuated.
The Paria River at Lees Ferry gauge (PFLA3) rose 4.36 feet in 30 minutes, peaking at 9.70 feet at 5:30 AM MST. Peak flow was 2446 cfs.

Major flooding occurred along the Nueces and Frio Rivers as a flood wave moved downstream following heavy rains over the southern Edwards Plateau. The Frio River near Derby was at Major flood stage between July 17 and July 19. ||Frio County did not experience significant damage, and no homes were affected by floodwaters. However, several highways were closed due to inundation as early as July 15, including US57, Highway 85, and several other county roads and farm-to-market highways. A water rescue involving a stranded tractor-trailer occurred on July 18 on FM117. Another water rescue…

Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding in Kerrville. Barricades were placed on 3rd and 4th Sts. and on Goat Creek Rd. at Junction Hwy. due to high water over the road. There was two feet of water on Coronado Dr. at Junction Hwy.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flooding. A vehicle stalled in water on FM 1863 at Cibolo Creek where up to four feet of water was flowing over the road.
Water completely covered the roadway along Evergreen Drive in West Little Rock.
A large amount of water covered Hermitage Road estimated to be between 1 to 2 feet deep with vehicles turning around due to the running water and depth of water over the roadway.
Widespread flash flooding was observed across southern Clearfield County. Numerous roads were under one to two feet of water, and there were multiple reports of cars trapped by high water.

Heavy rainfall across portions of southeast Minnesota and northeast Iowa resulted in increased runoff into the Upper Iowa River Basin. Consequently, downstream flow resulted in the Upper Iowa River at Bluffton to rise into flood stage during the morning on July 10th. The river crested in minor flood stage at 12.55 feet before falling below flood stage during the evening on July 10th.
High water covered Highway 67 near the Prescott County Club.
The roadway was flooded, and a tree was across the road at the intersection of Old Hartsville Road and Concord Church Road.
Route 322 was closed between the Middletown Road exit and Hersheypark Drive due to flooding.
Flash flooding reported along Fox Hollow Road near Toftrees, pushing debris onto the road and closing it.
Flooding on Maurus Street, with the road being washed out.
Numerous flooded roads and flooded basements in Johnsonburg.
The 911 call center reported high water reported near the intersection of Gayton Road and Broad Street in Henrico County.
The public reported flooding on the eastbound lanes of I-64 in Richmond via Waze.

The South Branch Tributary Mud Creek near Rauville went into flood on the afternoon of July 8th after heavy rainfall during the previous night and earlier that morning. A crest of 4.8 feet, 0.8 feet above flood stage was observed on the evening of July 8th, with minimal impacts before the creek dropped below flood during the afternoon of July 9th.
Flooding was reported on a portion of US Highway 14 in Fort Pierre.
Heavy rainfall of 2.55 inches caused widespread street flooding in Aberdeen, leading to stalled and abandoned vehicles.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding near Doss. RR 783 had two feet of water over it at Edwards Creek.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding northwest of Pipe Creek. Privilege Creek flooded the low water crossing at Old School Rd. and Privilege Creek Rd.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flooding closing Hwy 281 at Cibolo Creek.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flooding. Scull Crossing was partially washed out at Cibolo Creek.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. The Guadalupe River rose over the Sisterdale Rd. bridge.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. Red Bluff Creek flooded Hwy 16 east of Pipe Creek.
Flash flooding reported near 5th Street and Front Street in Tyler.
Numerous areas of street flooding reported along Broadway Avenue in downtown Tyler.
Report of vehicles stuck in flood waters near Hummel Avenue and South 10th Street.
Multiple flooded basements reported in the Hastings area near Deer Road and Miller Street.

Thompson Run came out of its bank, flowing across a portion of College Avenue and adjacent parking lots between Porter and Puddintown roads in College Township. At least one lane of traffic was closed on College Avenue.

The emergency manager reported heavy rain of 1 to 2 inches produced flash flooding, resulting in the police and fire departments responding to multiple stranded motorists along U.S. 66 between Ford Rd. and downtown Gallup, and on Maloney Ave. between 5th and 9th Streets. The Marshall's parking lot flooded near U.S. 491 and West Lincoln Ave with calf-high water, while water infiltrated the ground floor of the Rehoboth McKinley Christian Hospital.
Mount Pleasant Police Department reported Highway 17 south was down to only one lane due to flooding.
Charleston County dispatch reported approximately 2 feet of water in a grocery store parking lot near the intersection of the Isle of Palms Connector and Palm Boulevard.
High water covered portions of Bluepine Drive.
A photo showed a viaduct on Dixie Highway flooded and closed near Pine Road. Rainfall of 2.50 inches was reported near Homewood.
Street flooding was reported in multiple areas in Aurora.
Street flooding was reported in multiple areas in western Naperville.
Six inches of standing water was reported at Weber Road and Taylor Road.
Video showed several inches of standing water on a roadway in Joliet.

Multiple reports of flooding in Tuscaloosa along McFarland Boulevard and Paul Bryant Drive after 3 to 4 inches of rain fell in part of town. The McFarland Boulevard railroad underpass between 15th St and University Blvd was impassable, with several vehicles becoming stranded in water.
High water was reported just east of North Broadway, north of U.S. Route 50. Additionally, high water also covered portions of U.S. Route 50.
Several roads were reportedly flooded in the Hammond area.
Several streets were flooded near Bridgeview and Burbank.
Addison FD reported flooded roadways in the Addison and Lombard areas with cars stalled in floodwater.

Multiple reports of flooded roads, yards, and basements came out of southern Cook County in the vicinity of Tinley Park, Homewood, Harvey, and Midlothian. A stretch of I-57 was flooded near Markham. The underpass near the 147th St Metra station in Riverdale was flooded. One nearby rain gauge recorded over five inches of storm total rainfall, and another recorded over four inches.
Water was covering IL Route 53 in Lisle near Four Lakes Ave.
Sowerby Road in the town of Castile closed due to flooding.

Duck Creek below Whipple exceeded a bankfull level of 12 feet on the evening of July 21st. The creek reached a crest of 14.8 feet the next evening and then receded below bankfull early on the morning of the 23rd. As a result of the creek flowing out of its banks, low sections of OH Route 821 below Whipple flooded, as well as the intersection of Kohl Road and Whipple Run Road, Route 16 above Stanleyville, and agricultural fields next to the creek in and around Whipple.
Broadcast media relayed video of flash flooding along North Sherwood Forest Blvd near Florida Blvd.
Emergency management reported fire department responding to flooded vehicles along Crescent Drive near Trudeau Drive.
Emergency management reported fire department responding to flooded vehicles along Archery Drive near Woodcliff Drive.
Emergency management reported fire department responding to flooded vehicles along Airline Hwy near Victoria Drive.
Flash flooding reported near the intersection of Darrin Boulevard and Legion Hills Road.
Bellwood Street near Mike Carter Field in Tyler was flooded.
Flash flooding pushed water across Riggles Gap Sportsmen Road and an adjacent parking lot.
Several inches of water ponded on North Atherton Street adjacent to the Penn State Campus near the bus station.
Ponding of water on the roadway in the vicinity of East Charles Street and South Main Street.
Water is over Highway 60 in Johnstown at Lippitt Ave to 6 inches deep.
Running water of multiple inches in depth flowing over County Road 35.
Public reported, via Facebook, water running over roads near Steamboat Canyon golf course.
The Skull Valley Wash gauge (YSVA3) showed a rise of 2.5 feet by 1:42 PM.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding on western edge of Acoma Pueblo near the El Malpais Ranger Station.
Standing water was reported on CR-167 and Center Lake Rd.
Public reported via social media flooding near Keystone Ave. and Gear St.
High water from Cloverlick Creek was reported over Bethel New Hope Road near Elm Corner.
A photo showed flowing water 12 inches deep near McIntosh Avenue and Burlington Avenue.
Multiple streets were flooded around parts of La Salle and Peru.
Tyler Creek rose out of its banks causing extensive flooding at Judson University. Several local roads were flooded and impassable.

Flooding was reported around the west side of Elgin. Six to eight inches of standing water was reported at Lucca Dr. A nearby rain gauge recorded over 3.8 inches of rain, nearly all of that within one hour. At least one foot of standing water was reported on College Green Dr.
Several inches of water were flowing across Sandwich Rd at Jericho Rd in Hinckley.
Numerous yards and roads were flooded in North Aurora near and west of the Fox River.
Structure flooding was reported near Pine St and Hart Rd in Batavia.

Multiple flooding reports were received from Woodridge along and south of 75th St. 75 St was closed at Dunham Rd. Janes Ave and Lemont Rd were both closed south of 75th St due to flooding. Structure flooding was reported near 87th St and Havens Dr. One nearby rain gauge recorded nearly 5.2 inches of rain and another recorded over 4.5 inches, most of which fell within one hour.
Law enforcement reported some flooded roadways across Johnson City.
Law enforcement reported some flooded roadways across Greeneville.
Some flooded roadways between Jonesborough and Greeneville TN.
Handful of roads closed due to flooding rain in the Perry area.
Fulmer Valley Road closed down due to flooding.
Several roads closed down due to flooding including, Route 19, Route 248 and Dutch Hill Road.

Around 5 to 7 inches of rain fell in far eastern Nicollet County from the night of July 30th into the morning of July 31st. The heavy rainfall caused a small mudslide that briefly blocked the southbound lanes of US169 just north of St. Peter.
Highway 16 and College street in Lindale was closed due to flooding.
Reports of flash flooding along South State Street.
Residential flooding reported on Hillcrest Road.
Heavy rains produced flood waters over intersections in central Gallup, and over U.S. 491 just north of Gallup.
Several low lying areas of Sandwich were flooded. One picture shared showed several inches of standing water along Griswold Springs Rd just east of Duvick Ave.
Broadcast media reported a flooded underpass in Elmhurst.
Four inches of standing water was reported.
Fox Rd was flooded at Fox Glen Dr in Yorkville. Nearby yards were also flooded.

Multiple reports of flooding came out of the south and southeast sides of Frankfort. Roads, sidewalks, and yards were flooded near Laraway Rd and Harlem Ave. A car was stalled in floodwater along Pine Ridge Dr.

Multiple reports of flooding came out of the west side of Matteson. Multiple residential streets near Ridgeland Ave and Timber Ridge Rd were flooded. Inundation was estimated to be at least one foot in spots with water reaching sidewalks and yards. Structure flooding was reported near US Rt 30 and Harlem Ave.
A photo shared to social media showed standing water on the shoulder and across one southbound lane of I-57 near mile marker 331 just southwest of Harlem Ave.
IL Rt 1 was flooded south of Crete Monee Rd south of Crete.
Multiple roads were flooded in the vicinity of Edwards Hospital in Naperville. Washington Street at Gartner Rd was under water.

Numerous flash flood reports came out of the south side of Naperville near and south of 75th St. 75th St was flooded in spots with multiple adjacent roads and parking lots also under water. Wehrli Rd and Lisson Rd were flooded between 75th and 87th streets. A retention pond at Hunters Woods Park exceeded bankfull and flooded Naper Blvd as well as nearby yards.
VDOT reported standing water on I-95 at mile marker 82 in Henrico County.
The 911 call center reported standing water on Bell Creek Road.
VDOT reported standing water on I-95 at mile marker 81 in Henrico County. This flooding closed the north left shoulder, left lane, center lane, and right lane.
A trained spotter reported water crossing the road near the intersection of Hungary Road and Springfield Road.
VDOT reported flooding along Bestland Road.
Route 237 was closed due to flooding.
Traffic camera showing flooding of 2 lanes of I-390 at Henrietta Road.
Flooding of 2 to 4 inches over entirety of Culver Road and Melville Street intersection.
Residential flooding was reported on Akron Road.
Water rescue in the 300 block of West Main Street.
Water resuce reported near West Main Street and Granger Road.
Multiple flooded basements in residential structures (19 in total) and flooded roadways reported in the borough of Lewis Run.
Broadcast media live report shared on social media showed video of flooded roads on William Few Parkway near Windmill Plantation.
Deep water was ponding on parts of US-45 in Effingham.

A creek was overflowing and causing flooding on Carters Valley Rd near Lebanon United Methodist Church. Water was estimated to be about 4 inches deep. Moderate to heavy rain was occurring at the time.
DuPage County dispatch relayed that 5th St was flooded near Fairview Ave in Westmont with at least one car stalled.
Ditches and streams were flooded near the west branch of the DuPage River in West Chicago.

Numerous roads and yards were flooded around Carol Stream. The intersection at Paxton Pl and Shelburn Dr was flooded with six to twelve inches of water. Widespread inundation was reported across Armstrong Park.

Multiple flooding reports came out of the south side of Bartlett. Struckman Blvd was flooded between IL Rt 59 and Bartlett Rd with cars stalled. Sunset Park along Struckman Blvd was completely under water. Floodwater was up to car doors near Bartlett and Stearns roads. At least one foot of water was reported along Pickett Court. One rain gauge in the area recorded over 5.4 inches of rain in a six hour period, over 3.7 of which fell within one hour.
An underpass was flooded at Halstead St and 75th St in Chicago.
A handful of basement flooding reports came out of Chicago's Avalon Park, Calumet Heights, and South Chicago community areas.
Portions of the Edgebrook Country Club were flooded as water levels continued to rise along the Somonauk Creek following the rain into the morning of the 5th.
VDOT reported high water on the southbound lanes of US Route 13 in the vicinity of Parksley Road.
Social media pictures of flooding of residential streets in North Chili.
All lanes northbound closed due to flash flooding.
Traffic Cameras showing flooding of left lane on I-590 north of Blossom Road.
Residential flooding on Glenbrook Road.
Forest Hill Road closed due to flash flooding.
Geist Road closed due to high water.
Flash flooding in Lakewood led to some road closures.
Flash flooding was reported along Veterans Parkway and Babbit Lane. Flash flooding was also reported around Bradford Lane.
Significant flash flooding was reported on Lake Street in Asbury Park. Deal Lake drive was completely inundated and impassable.
Flash flooding was reported on State Rt. 57 and NJ 31.
Flash flooding on roadways and parts of I-40 across much of northeast and southeast Albuquerque.
Heavy rain from a thunderstorm resulted in floodwaters over roads in the northeast part of Zuni Pueblo, prompting closures of Old Gallup Road, Sandy Springs Road, and Lakeside Drive.
Numerous roads were closed in Danville due to water flowing across them.
US-45 was closed southeast of Flora due to water flowing across the road.

Report from Piute County Sheriff and Emergency Management that there were muddy flows in City Creek Canyon originating from the Cottonwood burn scar in Piute County. Approximately 0.3 to 0.7 inches of rain fell across portions of the upper City Creek drainage.
Flooding report received via mPING, with a photograph also sent via the X social media platform. Picture showed minor street and yard flooding.
Report of a Dodge Charger stuck in floodwaters near 275.
Trained spotter reported street and yard flooding. Depth was unknown.
A Knox county dispatcher noted two vehicles stuck in water near Western and Middlebrook with another report of a vehicle stuck near University and Western.
Flooding in a parking lot was hindering exit from business. There was also a report of flooding on nearby 5th avenue.
Heavy rain resulted in flooded roadways in the area of North Springfield Street and Industrial Drive in Saint James.
Route TT was closed both ways due to flooding over Crocked Creek near Sligo. It was reported closed the morning of July 10, but likely was flooded due to a rapid rise during the overnight hours.

Lake Holiday rose out of its banks as water levels continued to rise along the Somonauk Creek following the rain into the morning of the 5th. Water was inundating adjacent parks, beach areas, and residential yards.
A resident at a home on Warren Avenue was fatally electrocuted in high water. Two other individuals were injured by electrocution in high water, after attempting to assist the resident.
properties.epi: A stalled stationary boundary sparked showers and thunderstorms across the Ohio Valley region before eventually lifting north as a warm front. A very moist airmass was in place and storms produced heavy rainfall, leading to flooding.

properties.note: Road flooding was reported around the south side of Joliet near the Des Plaines River. IL Rt 53 was impassable near Doris Ave. Westbound lanes on Interstate 80 were under water near Center St.

A handful of road flooding reports came out of the vicinity of the Fox Valley mall. An underpass was flooded along IL Rt 59 south of Aurora Rd with other nearby roads also flooded. Another underpass was flooded along McCoy Dr east of Eola Rd. One nearby rain gauge recorded over five inches in 45 minutes, and another recorded nearly three inches in one hour.
Heavy rain from thunderstorms caused rapid runoff across US-93 from Main St. in Contact. Rocks and mud over the road which had to be plowed.
Several roads completely flooded around Henrietta area including Calkins Road and Jefferson Road.
Transit Road is closing down near the Lockport Plaza due to flooding.
Market Street was closed down due to flooding.

West Fork Duck Creek at Macksburg exceeded a bankfull level of 13 feet on the afternoon of July 21st. The creek reached a crest of 15.1 feet the next morning before receding below bankfull that evening. Impacts included flooding of a home and garage on Broad Street, the intersection of Broad Street and OH Route 821, the campground next to the gauge, Main Street near the creek, and agricultural fields adjacent to the creek.
Heavy rainfall caused irrigation canals along the Norwood River to overtop their banks. The flood remained over agricultural land and no major damage was reported.
Flooding occurred on Bear Mountain Road and Elk Creek Road.
High water was observed on Deepwater Mountain Road between Mount Carbon and Deep Water.
High water observed on Big Run at WV 18, Fink Creek Road, Alice Road between Shadow Dance Drive and Flat Run Road, and Leading Creek Road between Alice Road and Ellis Run Road.

Hickory Flat Run exceeded its banks near Walnut Drive. Significant flooding impacted homes on Morgan Addition Road, trapped residents in homes on Old Elkins Road, and stranded vehicles on Pinnell Street. A swift water rescue occurred on Little Sand Run and Bailey Ridge Road. Up to three feet of water flooded Stony Run Road near Route 20 South Road.
Flooding and water rescues were reported in the Buckhannon area. Impacted roads included US 33, Cleveland Avenue, Mud Lick Road, and Buckhannon Crossroads.
Multiple videos and pictures, sent in by the local fire department, showed flash flooding in Milford. Water rescues were needed.
Flash flooding was reported on NJ 57, in both Directions, west of Stephensburg Road (Mansfield Twp). All lanes were closed in the eastbound and westbound directions.
The Musconetcong River at Bloomsbury rose above flood stage.
The gauge along the Whippany River at Morristown rose above flood stage.
Cibecue Creek stream gauge (CBQA3) measured a 4.27 foot rise, with a peak flow of 2294 cfs.

A member of the public reported heavy rainfall in the area. As rain continued to fall, conditions progressively got worse with an mPING report indicating localized flash flooding. An emergency management coordinator later reported that the city of Navasota had multiple roads closed, severe road and culvert damage from heavy rainfall. The following roads were closed across the county: HWY 6 near J5 Tractor southbound, FM 1227 near HWY 6 at the railroad, FM 1774 near St. Marys, FM 3090 near FM 3455, FM 3455 between Fairgrounds and HWY 90, CR 227, CR 229, CR 318, CR 405, CR 406, CR 409, FM 2…
Heavy rain from a thunderstorm resulted in floodwaters over Lakeside Road and East Sandy Springs Road on the east side of Zuni.

Zion National Park dispatch reported flash flooding in Spry Canyon, Pine Creek, and the Overlook from earlier thunderstorms which produced heavy rain over those areas. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain was estimated to have fallen.
Hildale dispatch reported 1 to 1.5 feet of water in short creek which was confirmed by webcams. Short creek was dry prior to these reported flows.
Backcountry guide reported that Buckskin Gulch flashed at House Rock Valley Road and downstream to Buckskin Trailhead.
Ponding and standing water was reported on the Emory Road beneath the I-75 overpass, as well as on the on ramp for I-75 southbound.
Reports of flooding in the Henley Street Tunnel.
Law enforcement reported intersection of Murphy Ave and Vermont Ave was flooded.

Great Basin National Park Rangers reported of flash flooding with debris flow over State Route 487 and US-50 due to multiple days of heavy rain from monsoon thunderstorms. The roads were closed over the next several days with cleanup and repairs beginning on 7/22.

Multiple roads were flooded in Bolingbrook near and north of Boughton Rd between IL Rt 53 and Janes Ave. A nearby rain gauge recorded over 4.5 inches of rain, nearly all of which fell within one hour.

Multiple flooding reports were received from Bolingbrook near IL Rt 53 and Lily Cache Creek. Several roads and parking lots were flooded near Rt 53 and Lily Cache Ln. The creek rose above bankfull flooding a stretch of Briarcliff Rd and other roads near Brooks Middle School.
Numerous roads flooded around the Medina area.
Excessive runoff and storm drain backup from heavy rainfall producing flooding at the Orleans Community Health Hospital, with water now reaching into the lower level of the hospital.
Report of house flooded in Chesire.
Widespread flooding was occurring along Coursey Boulevard due to heavy rainfall.
Flash flooding occurred near and along the College Parkway in Parkersburg.
Flooding was observed on Pullman Drive and Northwest Turnpike.
High water was observed on Files Creek Road and at the intersection of Beverly Pike and Chenoweth Creek Road.
Flooding reported on Welsh Hill Road and Stutzmantown Road.
The Oak Creek gauge at Sedona (OAKA3) measured a 1.68 foot rise at 4:00 AM, then after a brief drop, measured a 2.2 foot rise at 8:00 AM. Maximum flow was 706.6 cfs.
The West Fork Oak Creek gauge (OAWA3) measured a 2.3 foot rise, or a peak flow of 171 cfs.
The Verde River near Clarksdale river gauge (VDCA3) measured a 3.22 feet rise, with a maximum flow of 898.7 cfs.
The Sycamore Creek above the Verde River stream gauge (SYMA3) rose 1.92 feet in 1 hour. Peak flow was 528 cfs.
The Moenkopi Wash Gauge (MOEA3) reported a rise of 6.31 feet in 15 minutes and rose a total of 8.52 feet in one hour. Peak flow was 1694 cfs.

Public reported flash flooding of Dry Creek in the Sunset Hill neighborhood with a bridge on Sunset Hills Drive being flooded over. Flood waters were black with ash from the Pocket Fire burn scar upstream. Times are estimated.
ADOT reported flooding over roadway on US-191 northbound near BIA road 9345.

Yavapai County Sheriff's Office reported Williamson Valley Road closed near the Chevron gas station by Interstate 40 due to flooding. A photo was sent of a stalled out vehicle in the flood waters. Time is estimated from radar.
The Snyder Fire Department reported flash flooding along several streets in the community of Snyder. The total time of occurrence is estimated from radar, and no damage was reported.
Pecos County Emergency Management reported street flooding in Fort Stockton, especially at low-water crossings. The total time of occurrence is estimated from radar, and no damage was reported.
Trained spotter reported flash flooding at the intersection of State Hwy 176 and FM 1212. The total time of occurrence is estimated from radar, and no damage was reported.

State DEM camera showed a debris flow flash flood wave moving down Beaver River within Cottonwood burn scar. Another subsequently showed debris flow flash flood wave continuing farther downstream in the Beaver River within the Cottonwood burn scar.

Video received via social media of muddy flows at Bald Mountain Pass. 1.81 inches of total rain fell at the nearby Bald Mountain Pass UDOT RWIS sensor, with 1.59 inches of rain falling in an hour. Time approximate.
The Iron County Emergency Manager shared a video of flash flooding on Kanarra Creek near Kanarra Falls.
The Beaver live camera number 3 showed an ongoing debris flow working down the drainage from the Cottonwood burn scar.

Very heavy rainfall from a nearly stationary supercell thunderstorm produced flash flooding across northeast Dundy County. Numerous county roads were washed out and impassable, and flood waters pushed a truck off the road into a ditch. There were no known injuries. Crop and property damage amounts are unknown.
Report of water coming over curbs. Heavy rainfall due to a thunderstorm.

Significant road flooding was reported along and south of 75th St in Darien. Several yards were flooded. Multiple cars were stalled and at least one structure was flooded near Plainfield Rd and Seminole Dr.

Mill Creek at Nolensville crested to 13.27 feet which was minor flood stage. At this stage, water flooded low-lying areas along the creek, including portions of Culbertson Road east of Nolensville Pike as well as walking trails near the Honey Brook subdivision. Water also approached Bluff Road west of Nolensville Pike.
I-55 was flooded between Lemont Rd and IL Rt 83. Parking lots were flooded near I-55 and Cass Ave. A portion of the main trail at Waterfall Glen washed out due to an unnamed creek flooding.
Received report on Facebook of water rescue with photo of vehicle stuck in flood waters on College Avenue.
Received report via mPING of roads closed due to flooding.
A picture on social media showed water 1-2 feet deep near the intersection of North Boulevard at Napoleon.
Street flooding in several locations in the city of DuBois.
Public reported, via Facebook, parts of Navajo Route 15 near Sunrise Springs flooded with debris on the road.
Public reported, via Facebook, water running over roads in Steamboat Canyon.
Town of Clarkdale's Facebook page reported South Broadway Road closed between Main Street and Centerville Road due to flood debris on the roadway.

Verde Independent reports flooding within the Clarkdale town hall. 87 gallons of water were pumped from inside the building. South Broadway covered with mud from flooding, reducing travel to a single lane. Time is estimated.
Video on Facebook from the Verde Independent of flooding across a low water crossing along Camino Real near Fir Street in Cottonwood.
Tonto Creek stream gauge (TNRA3) measured a 4.22 foot rise. Times are estimated.
Cooper Hills Road in Globe closed due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries reported.
Beer Tree Crossing in Globe impassable due to flooding from Pinal Creek. No damages or injuries reported.

USGS gauge located along Pinto Creek recorded 10 ft rapid rise, impacting downstream low water crossings. Another USGS gage along Pinto Creek downstream recorded 7.5 ft rise. No damages or injuries reported.
An off-duty NWS employee reported flash flooding in Gardendale. 0.8 inches of rain fell in approximately 15 minutes. The total time of occurrence is estimated from radar, and no damage was reported.
Public report of flash flooding on Louisiana Avenue in Midland. The total time of occurrence is estimated from radar, and no damage was reported.
A public report was received from an MPING of flash flooding on North Midland Drive. The total time of occurrence is estimated from radar, and no damage was reported.
Broadcast media relayed a picture from the public of flash flooding in Monahans. The total time of occurrence is estimated from radar, and no damage was reported.
USGS stream gauge on the Santa Clara River recorded a flood wave with flows increasing from approximately 4 cfs to 240 cfs in roughly 1 hour. Time is coincident with observed peak flow.
A USGS gauge on Leads Creek showed a rise of 1.5 feet, indicating a flash flood.

Flash flooding reported on Copper Gulch Road in south-central Fremont County near the county line near Custer County. Fremont County Emergency Management reports two to 3 feet of water with two to three feet of debris and mud in the 8000-9000 block of Copper Gulch Road.
State DEM webcam showed a debris flow flash flood wave continuing downstream in the Beaver River within the Cottonwood burn scar.
The USGS stream gauge on the Santa Clara River at Pine Valley rose 1.5 feet, from just 4 CFS to 101 CFS.

Zion National Park reported many slot canyons and dry washes are flash flooding. Subsequently, the USGS river gauge at North Fork Virgin River spiked from about 30 cfs to 290 cfs with a flash flood wave.
The Garfield County Sheriff Office reported flash flooding in Castro Canyon. Time estimated.
A member of the broadcast media shared a photo of ponding of water on a roadway in Ahoskie.
Heavy rain in the Lawrenceburg area caused flooding on Fall River Road from near the intersection of Baker Lane to Highway 64. Extent of damages is unknown.

Numerous flooding reports came out of Willowbrook and Burr Ridge east of IL Rt 83. All lanes of I-55 between IL Rt 83 and County Line Rd were under water. Multiple cars were stalled along I-55 east of Rt 83. Cars were also stalled along 83rd St east of Madison St. Plainfield Rd was flooded near Rt 83.
Multiple evacuations occurring, including houses on Dutch Hill Road and Schrader Road.
A water rescue on Dutch Hill Road in Willing.
Received report via mPING of roads closed due to flooding.
Multiple videos from the Chrysotile area showed significant flow in Ash Creek, impacting a road crossing the creek. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries reported.
Forest Ave unbridged crossing between Highway 60 and Sullivan St was closed due to flooding from Bloody Tanks Wash. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries reported.
Broadcast media relayed a picture from the public of flash flooding on roadways in Kermit. The total time of occurrence is estimated from radar, and no damage was reported.

Broadcast media relayed a picture from the public of flash flooding at the intersection of Wadley and Ward in Midland. The total time of occurrence is estimated from radar, and no damage was reported.
HAM radio operator reported that the intersection of Highway 349 and CR 130 is underwater. The total time of occurrence is estimated from radar, and no damage was reported.
Public report from MPING of flash flooding of streets and roads in West Odessa. The total time of occurrence is estimated from radar, and no damage was reported.
There was a report of 4 to 6 inches of water flowing across southbound U.S. Highway 491 just north of Gallup. Location was estimated based on radar.

Multiple reports from Beulah Fire, Emergency Mgt and Public:||Highway 78 near Beulah with large amounts of debris from the Aspen Acres burn scar. ||Wall of water/debris flow coming down squirrel creek sending small structure down creek taking out power poles and propane tanks.||Mud and debris overflowing culvert over the road.||Mud and debris flow through Beulah. Multiple homes flooded. Bridges and roads closed and not structurally sound due to flooding.
Received a trained spotter video of a very large flood wave near US-89 on the Paria River.

Photos and video on social media show flash flooding of normally dry washes around Tropic, along with a report of nearly 2.5 inches of rain in rain gauge in Tropic. Additionally, the Garfield County Sheriff Office reported many dry washes flooding around Kodachrome Basin State Park and Tropic.
Roadway flooding was reported approximately one mile south of the intersection at Jericho and Granart roads south of Big Rock.
A doorbell camera showed a portion of Circle Drive in Boulder Hill completely flooded with water rising up to residents lawns.
Three feet of standing water was reported at IL-47 and Galena Rd south of Sugar Grove.
Law Enforcement reported that Western Avenue was closed due to water over the road. There were several other roads with water over them as well.
Assisted water rescue on Rose Road in Angelica.
A total of 6 water rescues performed across the county during the late afternoon hours.
Reports of several homes needing cellar pumping in the Village of Perry. One structure had a wall compromised.
California Highway Patrol reports water flowing over Nipton Road at the Interstate 15 on- and off-ramps. Multiple vehicles became stuck in the mud.
The Needles Underpass live stream shows multiple feet of water flowing under the Needles Underpass, with water approaching nearby homes and buildings.
Washes near the area of Tomahawk Road and Apache Trail in Apache Junction were running full with water flowing over the roadway, stranding a vehicle. No damages or injuries reported.
Tatum Blvd between Jomax Rd and Dynamite Blvd closed due to flooding. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries reported.

Desert Hills Dr between 15th Ave and 19th Ave as well as 19th Ave between Desert Hills Dr and Irvine Rd were both closed due to flooding along Skunk Creek. A Maricopa County Flood Control District Steam Gauge along Skunk Creek at Desert Hills Drive showed water levels rising above the alarm stage level of 1.5 feet and peaking at 2.58 feet (562 cfs). Timing was estimated based on the period water levels exceeded and then receded below the alarm stage. No damages or injuries reported.
Apache Trail low water crossing in Tortilla Flat impassable due to flooding in Tortilla Creek. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries reported.
A USGS gauge on Bill Williams River measured a rapid 6 ft rise, with a peak of 5000 cfs, and came within 0.50 feet of the gauge's historical peak. No damages or injuries reported.
A USGS gauge along Sycamore Creek just west of SR-87 measured a rapid 3 foot rise and making Forest Service Road 402, a low-water crossing, impassable. No damages or injuries reported.
Law enforcement reported about one foot of water over the road on FM2400 near TX 349. The total time of occurrence is estimated from radar. No damage was reported.
Emergency managers reported flooding inside a home in the Viewpoint neighborhood. Floodwaters also knocked down a concrete block wall.

Yavapai County reported flooding in northern Prescott Valley, near Roundup Drive between Viewpoint Drive and Robert Road, as well as areas north of Spouse Drive. Other roads in the area had flood debris and standing water. An apartment complex had 13 residents displaced due to flooding.
The stream gauge on Bright Angel Creek below Cottonwood Campground (BAPA3) recorded a 2.91 ft rise.

Park Service employee observed Sulphur Creek flashing behind the Capitol Reef NP Visitor Center between 5PM and 520PM. Also, water was flowing across the Scenic Drive near Grand Wash Road at 335PM, and a dry wash parallel to SR24 at Sulphur Bridge had a flow entering the creek at 415 PM MDT.
Flash flood reported via emergency management where Chute Canyon crosses Wild Horse Road.
The Emergency Manager reported that multiple roads in Spring Valley were closed due to water over the road.
The Emergency Manager reported that several roads were closed due to high winter in town.
A trained spotter reported street flooding in the vicinity of Lem Turner Rd and Palmdale Street.
A few feet of standing water was reported along a residential street off of Big Timber Rd in Gilberts.
About one foot of standing water was reported on Reinking Rd near Higgins Rd in Pingree Grove. A nearby rain gauge recorded 5.6 inches of rain in roughly two hours.
Flooding was reported at the intersection of Sleepy Hollow Rd and Boncosky Rd in Sleepy Hollow.

properties.near: 2.07 SE Casa De Aero Park Airport
properties.note: A few inches of standing water were reported along Big Timber Rd near Prairie Ridge.
Multiple roads and yards were flooded on the southeast side of Big Rock near the Big Rock Forest Preserve.

Extensive road and creek flooding was reported around Big Rock along and south of US Rt 30. The east branch of Big Rock Creek flooded and inundated Hinckley Rd near Plowman's Park. Welch Creek flooded and numerous nearby roads were impassable including Granart Rd, Dauberman Rd, and Rt 30.
Multiple roads were flooded and closed around Sugar Grove and Prestbury.

Fast moving water moved out of the banks of Oak Arroyo Wash and flowed over Old Gallup Road, Lakeside Drive and Sandy Springs Road. Residents near Old Gallup Road experienced flooding requiring the use of sandbags. Flow moved more into Zuni Pueblo towards Highway 53 but water did not cover the road.
Sheriff reported that there was a flash flood ongoing in City Creek that remained within its banks. This flood originated from the Cottonwood burn scar.
The Marysvale Emergency manager reported a debris flow in Bullion Canyon with flood waters making it under the US-89 bridge. This debris flow originated from the Cottonwood burn scar.
A culvert partially collapsed due to flooding along Scott Rd between Dauberman Rd and Dagan Rd northwest of Sugar Grove.

Numerous roads and yards were flooded around the north side of Aurora. Indian Creek was flooded and inundating Broadway St. Debris was flowing in the floodwater. Garfield Park was flooded with water spilling over a berm into yards. Six to seven inches of water were reported near the Belles Terres apartment complex. Roads and parking lots were flooded along Marywood Ave south of Molitor Rd. One nearby rain gauge recorded over four inches of rain within one hour.
Van Emmon St was washed out due to flooding near Mill St in Yorkville.
NY Route 417 flooded on the west side of Allegany. Location approximated. The flood waters had receded by 5 AM EDT on July 28th.
Niagara County 911 Dispatch relayed report of heavy flooding just north of Center Street in Lewiston. Location approximated.
Barriers set up to close portions of North Main Street due to flooding.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms over the South Fork burn scar resulted in flash flooding and debris flows on and downstream of the burn scar. Fast flowing water, mud, and tree debris in the Cedar Creek basin flowed over Cedar Creek Drive, Cree Meadows Drive, Paradise Canyon Drive, Hull Road, and Eagle Drive. In the Upper Canyon neighborhood, floodwaters with mud and debris crossed Brady Canyon Road at Mechem, the first bridge at Main Road, and washed out the bridge at Riverside Drive trapping 3 permanent residents.
Flash flooding over a low water crossing of N. Brown Road through Berrendo Creek in northwestern Roswell, NM. Barricades were set up to prevent drivers from passing through the flood waters.
The USGS gauge on the Santa Clara River near Pine Valley rose 3 feet in 15 minutes due to a flood wave moving down the river.
USGS gauge showed a rise on Leads Creek of one foot as a result of flash flooding.

USGS stream gauge on the Green River at San Rafael recorded a flood wave as flow increased from 0 cfs to 693 cfs in less than 3 hours. Flows originated from slot canyons and washes on an earlier flash flood warned storm upstream over the San Rafael Swell.
The USGS gauge on the Santa Clara River above Baker Dam rose 2.5 feet in 15 minutes as a result of a flash flood wave moving down the river.
Emery County Emergency Management reported a flash flood and associated closure of WR-31 at Huntington Canyon near milepost 29.
A large flash flood wave was observed on North Creek, originating from the Cottonwood burn scar.
The Paria Contact Station reported flash flooding within Buckskin Gulch and Wire Pass.
Trained spotter video received from showing a large flow moving through the Paria River toward Buckskin Gulch. Time and location are approximate.
Trained spotter video received from showing a large flow moving through Buckskin Gulch. Time and location are approximate.
The USGS river gauge Paria River near Kanab reported a large flash flood wave from 2 CFS to 2630 CFS, a rise of nearly 6 feet.
Rushing water was reported across Inke Road.

Roads and yards were flooded along Elm St near US Rt. 30 in Waterman. Water was estimated to be at least a few feet deep and was up near some houses. A nearby rain gauge recorded over 4 inches of rain.
Social media report and photo of a culvert washed out with road impassable in Limestone.

Multiple flooding reports came out of the northwest side of Carol Stream. Flooded basements were reported near County Farm Rd and Schick Rd. Near County Farm Rd and Lies Rd, a retention pond overflowed and flooded nearby streets, lots, and yards. Fair Oaks Rd was also flooded near Big Horn Trl. A rain gauge in the area recorded 6.75 inches of rain, most of which fell in less than two hours.
A video on the TXDOT Facebook page showed several inches of water flowing across FM 2129 near Sonora.
A road was closed due to flash flooding.
Several road closures due to flash flooding, including Hwy 377, FM 479, FM 2169 and RR 385.
US HWY 380 is closed due to flash flooding.
Sago Road flooded.
A portion of South Spring Street flooded.
Roads flooded near Lost Creek.
In Dry Branch, high water was observed around the 700 block of Dry Branch Road.
Flooding was observed on Goffs Road.
The report was relayed via mPING.
Homeowner along Lobo Creek Road reported between 5 to 18 inches of standing water on the north side of the property after the adjacent arroyo overflowed from heavy runoff.

Burn scar flash flooding over the Salt burn scar impacted parts of Hollywood and Ruidoso Downs, including up to a foot of water and debris flowing down Glade Drive, closing the road. A stretch of U.S. Highway 70 between Hollywood and Ruidoso Downs was closed due to flash flooding and debris flows.
U.S. Route 35 and Quinn Road were closed by law enforcement due to high water. Additionally, several sections of State Route 503 were closed due to high water.
Area webcams and social media posts showed Short Creek overtopping its banks and the culvert at Hilldale Street.
A backcountry guide reported flash flooding in Buckskin Gulch and Wire Pass.

The Washington County Emergency Manager reported flash flooding, the highest occurring from the burn scar over the course of the strongly monsoonal influenced prior week. Flood waters covered the road in Pine Valley and encroached around structures in town, including the fire station.
The USGS Paria River Gauge spiked to 1460 CFS from less than 10 CFS with a flash flood wave.
Public submitted video of large debris flow flash flood pushing through the Shurtz Creek drainage associated with a thunderstorm.
Rushing water was reported across State Route 227 near Middleboro Lane.
Two to three feet of rushing water was observed over the roadway.
High standing water was reported over Waterfall Road near Chester Boulevard.
Independence Drive at Ventura Avenue in Homewood was flooded after heavy rainfall.
Media reported several roads flooded and impassable due to flooding, including FM 89 at County Road 654. County Road 272, and County Road 323.
Sutton County Emergency Manager reported evacuations and swift water rescues are being conducted in Sonora.
Crockett County Sheriffs Office reported at least 5 feet of flood water in the town of Ozona.
Crockett County Emergency Manager reported evacuations and swift water rescues being conducted in Ozona as well as flooding in homes.
Eldorado Fire Chief reported multiple county roads and farm to market roads closed. Reported 5 feet of water deep on one of the low water crossings. Highway 277 South closed due to flooding.
Eldorado Fire Chief reported 1 inch of water inside home. Also, there was 5.5 inches of rainfall in the last 24 hours.
Crockett County Sheriffs Office reports at least 12 evacuations from homes and businesses. In addition, there has been at least 1 medical evacuation. Swift boat teams continue to do water rescues.
The road was washed out by floodwaters at the intersection of Brownsville Road and Camp Road near Mill Creek.

Valley Chapel Road in Lewis County flooded in multiple locations from Freemans Creek. Several graveled side roads, including driveways and oil and gas access roads, washed out. Multiple homes had large amounts of standing water surrounding them.
A portion of US Route 33, near the Lewis County line, flooded on all lanes.

The West Fork River at Weston exceeded a flood stage of 17 feet on the evening of July 21st, and then rose to a crest of 18.8 feet before falling back below flood stage later that night. While the river was out of its banks, flooding of River Avenue occurred.

The West Fork River above Clarksburg exceeded a flood stage of 14 feet on the morning of July 22nd and then rose to a crest of 17.2 feet that afternoon. The river then fell back below flood stage that night. While the river was out of its banks, Baltimore Street, River Road, Liberty Avenue, Route 19, and low-lying areas along the river flooded. A water rescue occurred on Good Hope Pike and high water was also observed on Shinnston Pike.

The Tygart Valley River at Philippi exceeded a flood stage of 19 feet just after midnight on July 22nd. The river rose to a crest of 22.3 feet early the next morning and then fell back below flood stage during the afternoon. Numerous areas flood when the river rises out of its banks, including North High and Woods Streets, Stevens and Walnut Streets, a nearby store, Chestnut and McCartney Streets, Vietnam Veterans Park, the intersection of US Route 119 and Truck Route 250, Sycamore Street, and Beech Avenue.
Flooding reported via Streetwise at Kabel Dr and Macarthur Blvd.
Report of several inches of water on Bienville Street, reaching the sidewalks in a few spots.
Several inches of standing water on Canal St between Treme St and Marais St.
Heavy rain from a thunderstorm produced flash flooding and debris over Forest Service Road 107 along the Rio Bonito from Bonito Lake to Highway 37, likely contributed to by the 2022 Blue 2 burn scar.
Beaver County Emergency Management officials reported flash flooding in Beaver River and North Creek.
High water was reported over portions of U.S. Route 25.
High water was reported over Turner Road and Lincoln Ridge Road near Fork Lick Creek.
Six to eight inches of standing water was reported along Plainfield Road.
Photos showed several inches of water on roadways and in parking lots near Butterfield Road.
Several streets were closed due to flooded roadways in Addison.

Flooding occurred in several areas in southeast Lake County. A traffic camera showed several inches of water on Washington Street at the Interstate 94 underpass. Flooding was reported on Washington Street near Route 21 and along Grand Avenue on the east side of Gurnee. Flooding was reported on Green Bay Road north of Belvidere Road. A vehicle was stalled in flood waters at the Route 176 viaduct under Sheridan Road. Significant flooding was reported on Audrey Nixon Boulevard at Sheridan Road in Lake Bluff. The Port Clinton Parking Garage in Highland Park experienced flooding and was closed.…
The city of Mount Vernon had street flooding with water over the roadway at Hickory Street and Division Street.

Thunderstorms brought locally heavy rain to the area with private weather stations in South Sioux City indicating as much as 1.5 to 2 inches of rain fell in less than an hour. This resulted in street flooding across portions of the city, including in the 1400 block of B street as well as portions of G street.
The East FM 2169 has at The Bogs has become impassable.
Public reported low water crossing flooded at County Road 206 and Epps Creek.
At least a foot of standing water was reported along George Ct in Plainfield. Water was up to sidewalks and residents' yards.
Victory lane was flooded near Park Ave in Justice.
Roads, yards, and sidewalks were flooded around Hickory Hills.
A stretch of Cicero Ave was flooded near State Rd south of Midway Airport.
Roads were reported flooded near Marquette Park in Chicago.
An underpass along I-57 at 111th St was flooded.
Fast flowing water was observed over Cats Creek Road.
The intersection of Snook Road and State Route 668 flooded.

The Middle Fork Tygart Valley River at Audra exceeded a bankfull level of 10 feet on the night of July 21st. The river continued rising to a crest of 13.8 feet early the next morning before receding back below bankfull prior to midday. Impacts while the river was out of its banks included flooding of the campground and roads in Audra State Park.

The Middle Fork Tygart Valley River at Ellamore exceeded a bankfull level of 13 feet on the night of July 21st. The river reached a crest of 22.9 feet shortly after midnight and then receded back below bankfull later that morning. Impacts during this time included flooding of County Route 28.
The West Fork River at Enterprise exceeded a bankfull level of 17 feet on the afternoon of July 22nd. The river reached a crest of 17.1 feet before receding back below bankfull that same evening.

Middle Island Creek at Little exceeded a bankfull level of 14 feet on the morning of July 22nd. The creek then rose to a crest of 16.3 feet before receding back below bankfull that same evening. Impacts while the creek was out of its banks included flooding of low areas along secondary roads near the creek.

South Fork Hughes River below Macfarlan exceeded a bankfull level of 22 feet on the morning of July 22nd. The river reached a crest of 23.5 feet before receding back below bankfull that afternoon. Impacts that are often seen when the river rises to this level include flooding of low sections of Oxbow Road and agricultural fields.
Two feet of high water was observed at the intersection of Route 20 and Turkey Run Road.
Coursey near Sherwood forest was flooded due to heavy rainfall.

Emergency management reported flash flooding and debris over the roadway on the northern fringe of the South Fork burn scar along Eagle Creek impacting areas along Highway 532 to the Gavilan Canyon Rd. at the intersection with NM 48.
A trained spotter reported flood waters were flowing over a 2 to 3 inch road curb, across the sidewalk, and into Santi's Restaurant at the intersection of Ben Sawyer Boulevard and Center Street.
Charleston County dispatch reported Cameron Boulevard is flooded and impassable from 36th Avenue and 41st Avenue on Isle of Palms.
Charleston County dispatch reported Park West Boulevard was closed due to flooding. A few vehicles were flooded and stalled on Park West Boulevard near Highway 17.
Emergency Management installed camera detected a flash flood on the North Creek drainage of the Cottonwood burn scar.
The parking lot of a local school was submerged in standing water.

Max Creek Road was impassible, with 2 of the 7 bridges leading into Camp Powhatan sustaining damage. The estimated water depth in Big Macks Creek was 9 feet higher than base flow. Debris was observed having been washed onto some of the bridges. Runoff caused Lake Powhatan to rise 3 to 4 feet.
A portion of roadway was washed out by rushing water near the intersection of Mason Lewis Road and Kelsey Street.
Jacksonville Sheriff's Office reported multiple vehicles stuck in floodwaters near Broadway Ave and W Beaver St as well as near State St and Acorn St. Broadway Ave near W Beaver St was closed.
There were flood waters inundating a residence in Wahiawa.
Water rescue of a stranded motorist in deep water near Iowa street.
Thunderstorm rainfall up to 2.50 inches in under 1.5 hours produced flash flooding, stranding cars in northeastern Sullivan County.
Cow Creek Road was washed out due to flash flooding. A picture showed Frog Alley, off Cow Creek Road, underwater with water halfway up the sides of UTVs and underneath trailers.

North Sand Branch left its banks and flooded North Sand Branch Road. On Upper Rock Creek Road, a house and yard flooded, the road flooded, and flood waters were strong enough to push an SUV. McDowell Hollow Road was closed due to flash flooding. Sections of Route 3 between Whitesville and Glen Daniel also flooded.
Water entered a home on Blair Mountain Highway.

SEMA reported that a motorist was stranded in their vehicle near County Road 281 and 234 between the North River and Big Branch River. The water was about knee deep. The individual was unharmed. The North River rising out of its banks impacted other roads, including County Road 324 and 230.
Water rescue of motorist stalled on Golden Avenue in flood waters.
Motorists were rescued when their vehicle stalled in over a foot of water on Topeka Blvd.
Flooding was reported in buildings along Brotherton Road.
A vehicle was in floodwater at Lumley Road and Appling Way.
Flash flooding was reported. Vehicles were stranded.
Temple FD reported road closures in the city due to flooding that include Charter Oak Drive south of Kegley Road, portions of Riverside Drive, and W Abrams and SH317.
Flash flooding was reported. Roads were closed. Vehicles were inundated.

Rain began at about 10PM on the 9th, but heavy rain continued through most of the night. Flash flooding began in the early morning hours, peaking before dawn. By morning, a swath of 7 to 10 inches of rain had fallen across southwest Madison County. All creeks and rivers in this area overflowed their banks, with most of this water flowing through the St Francis River. Some roads were inundated including Route C near Saco.
Nogales PD vehicle impacted by flash flooding at Nogales Wash. Time estimated.
A vehicle stalled in floodwaters on North Cascabel Rd and East Glory Hill rd. Time estimated based on radar and report.
A vehicle was stranded in flood waters along Glenwood Avenue near the intersection with Kodiak Drive.
Terrell Volunteer Fire Department reported flooding in Terrell, with vehicles stuck in high water near the intersection of Texas Highway 34 and High Street.
The flood waters caused a culvert to be washed out, making the CR 50S between 120W and 110W impassable.
A culvert was washed out on CR 30N between 100W and 90W due to the long duration torrential rainfall.
A culvert was washed out on CR 40N between 130W and 140W.
Heavy rain caused flooding along Taylor Chapel Road south of Dover with portions of the road washed away. Damages are a rough estimate.
The Teague Fire Department conducted a water rescue of an 18 wheeler on Highway 164.

Flash flooding due to heavy rainfall closed several roads and impacted residences in Curtice due to creeks and streams overflowing their banks. Impacted roadways include portions of State Route 579 including the intersection of Nissen Road. Numerous homes in Curtice experienced yard flooding and several homes experienced basement flooding.

The county emergency manager reported that flooding was beginning on some roads in the Brackney to Silver Lake area. 2.5 inches of rain was reported to have fallen in 90 minutes at the Silver Lake gauge location.

Rain began at about 10PM on the 9th, but heavy rain continued through most of the night. Flash flooding began shortly after midnight, peaking just before dawn. By morning, a swath of 5 to 7 inches of rain had fallen across the southern portion of the county from Courtois to Belgrade. Most creeks and rivers in this area overflowed their banks. Water was reported over the road in numerous locations along Highway C.

Water rescues and road closure signs were needed by the Dollar General and Victory Valley Church on Veterans Memorial Highway. A vehicle went under water in the middle of a road, and the driver was observed standing on the top.

Photo showed a pickup truck stranded in the floodwaters along Gilson Wash near San Carlos River. Water was around 2 ft deep with the truck's tires fully submerged. The driver was able to escape the vehicle. Timing estimated from post and radar. No injuries reported.
Water entered the first floor and basements of several homes along Corwin Road near Oregonia.

Flash flooding was reported over portions of northeast Brazoria county. Flash flooding was initially reported by the member of the public, who estimated around 4 inches of standing water in Hillcrest. A storm chaser shared a video on social media showing flooding over portions of Alvin. In the video, extensive inundation can be seen across two residential properties with both homes surrounded by water. One property had water over the front porch, reaching the front door. Flash flooding onset was estimated from gauge and radar observations. Another video shared by storm chasers showed other…

Heavy rainfall caused a creek to overflow in Sector Paracaochero near Camino Los Cruces in San Juan. Flash floodwaters inundated two residential units near Aceros de Am��rica, resulting in flood damage to the affected properties. No injuries or fatalities were reported.
Over a foot of standing water inundated at least eleven cars at a local car dealer and portions of the corner gas station. Several homes also had water over their porches, up to their front doors.
Report with pictures of flooding that washed out a roadway and a culvert pipe on River Road east of Gateway. There was debris on the roadways as well from flood waters.
Bunker Hill Road washed out.

Mann Road was flooded from Spring Lake Road to the Marion County line from up to 3.25 inches of rainfall, with a deer rescued next to an inundated car. The water crossing Mann Road near the car was nearly 2 feet deep. Landersdale Road also flooded east of Paddock Road as did Cox Road north of Landersdale Road.
Flooded roads across the county. Total rainfall for the event was around 2.5 inches.
Flooded roads across the county. Total rainfall for the event was around 2 inches.

Multiple sources reported flash flooding developed along Buffalo Creek after 2.5 to 4 inches of rain fell in the area where Caldwell, Watauga, and Wilkes Counties come together. Water from the creek inundated a portion of Stone Mountain Rd. The bridge at Camp Carrolwood Rd was reportedly overtopped, while several culverts were washed out along lower portions of Buffalo Cove Rd.
Social media pictures and videos of cars stuck in flooded roads in downtown Milwaukee. DOT cameras show a few locations with cars stuck in water at highway underpasses.

Excessive rainfall created a significant rise and subsequent flooding along the Tioughnioga River near Cortland, NY. The streamgage crested at 10.37 feet during the afternoon of April 1st. The river exceeded the Moderate flood stage which is 10 feet. The main road between Cortland and Marathon was flooded and closed for hours.

High water has been reported on State Road 67 in the area of Thompson Road and Coon Hunter Road, southwest of Bruceville, and along with Coon Hunter Road itself. Total rainfall for the event was around 2 inches.
