Fast flowing water in streets was between 2 and 3 feet high at|the…
Standing water caused vehicles to become stranded on roads with at least one road closed by the high water.
Multiple roads were flooded in Breaux Bridge and Cecelia and some were impassable with cars stalled. Water also briefly entered Saint Martin Hospital in Breaux Bridge.
Numerous roads closed due to flooding in Terre Haute and points to the south in Vigo County.
A section of the roadway was washed out due to flooding near the intersection of Southwest 174th Street and Market Road. The event time is approximate.
A culvert collapsed from the heavy rainfall on B Highway leading to road closure.

Heavy rain from slow-moving thunderstorms caused rises along Berry Creek. The combination of elevated streamflow and accumulation of water in a nearby detention basin led to a washout across both lanes of Berry Creek Drive between Airport Road/Briarcrest Drive and Mourning Dove Boulevard.
A car was stuck in floodwaters near the intersection of Lynn Road and Glenwood Avenue. Fire department was on the scene to provide a water rescue.

Tooele County Parks and Recreation reported that Butterfield Canyon Road on the Salt Lake Valley side was closed due to being washed out from rain. Rainfall estimates are approximately 0.7 inches from a weather station near Kennecott mine.
Water flowing across multiple roads south of Terre Haute.
Emergency management reported multiple instances of standing water on roads in Austin and that a vehicle was stuck in a flooded roadway on Interstate 90.
The DOT reports NY 9J is closed due to flash flooding between Day Road and County Route 26A in Stuyvesant.
The DOT reports NY 9J is closed due to flash flooding between Day Road and County Route 26A in Stuyvesant.
The DOT reports NY 9J is closed due to flash flooding between Gibbons Road and School House Road in Stuyvesant.
The DOT reports NY 9J is closed due to flash flooding between Gibbons Road and School House Road in Stuyvesant.
NY Route 9J was closed between Seaman Avenue and Hamilton Way in the Town of Schodack due to flash flooding.
NY Route 9J was closed between Seaman Avenue and Hamilton Way in the Town of Schodack due to flash flooding.
Reported 4.47 inches of rainfall in a 2 hour period. EM estimated 5-6 homes off of William Few Parkway were inundated with water levels exceeding that of 9/26/24, the day before Helene.
Vehicles were reported stranded in Mantoloking.
Cars were stranded and water rescues were needed in Parsippany and Troy Hills.
Cars were stranded and water rescues were needed in Boonton.

A twelve-mile stretch of SR-88, between Mileposts 228-240, closed due to flooding damage sustained from 2-3 inches rain that fell the night of the 16th and the morning of the 17th. Flood damage included rockfalls, clogged culverts and drains, and portions of the road that were washed away. This stretch of the road was closed for approximately one week for repairs. Timing of impacts on the 16th estimated from radar. No injuries reported.
Rushing water washed out multiple culverts near Wallace Road and State Route 227.
A culvert at Long Run Road washed out and the road was covered with water and logs.
One foot in depth of water flowing across old 40 highway and Deer road in between Abilene and Solomon.
Depth of water is 3.5 feet flowing over road at 5th and Cedar road. Numerous roads have flowing water over them. Highways K15 and 5th street had 10 inches of flowing water over the road.
North Beechwood Street flooded with water almost halfway up the side of multiple cars.
Old highway 40 is impassable due to flood waters.
Widespread flooding is occurring on multiple roadways throughout Abilene.
Portions of E 91st Street S were flooded near S 145th East Avenue, and several vehicles were stranded in the flood water.
Significant flash flooding was reported in Eatontown. Roads were flooded. Vehicles were half submerged in the water.
A public social media post showed portions of Old Coffee Road washed out due to flood waters near Fitzgerald Highway in the vicinity of the Coffee/Irwin County border.

Public reports 3 or 4 stalled out cars on I-20 westbound between FM1788 and Loop 338 exits heading into Odessa. Video of flash flooding was also shared on social media. The total time of occurrence is estimated from radar and from the time of the initial reports. The cost of damages is also estimated.

Local media reported that heavy rainfall during the afternoon of the 18th caused multiple flooded homes in Nu'uuli village. An American Samoa Power Authority/University of Hawaii stream gauge in the village rapidly rose to over three times its initial height in a single hour. Fiscal damage is estimated.

Local media reported that heavy rainfall during the afternoon of the 18th caused multiple flooded homes in Pava'ia'i village. The nearby A'asu Village American Samoa Power Authority/University of Hawaii Mesonet station recorded 2.86 inches of rainfall between 1 PM and 2 PM along with other heavy rainfall in the previous 3 days. Monetary damage is estimated.

An ice jam near the mouth of the Yuki River released a massive surge of water. As this front surged past Galena and Koyukuk, the Galena river gauge recorded a minor flood crest of 124.8 feet on May 15, before slowly receding into action stage (123.7 feet) by May 17.
Local media reported that heavy rainfall during the afternoon of the 18th caused multiple flooded homes in Faga'itua village. Monetary damage is estimated.
Local media reported that heavy rainfall during the afternoon of the 18th caused multiple flooded homes in Ottoville village. Monetary damage is estimated.

South Fork Palouse River flooding, with minor to moderate flooding in areas across Pullman, including downtown, Grand Avenue, and the area around the City Playfields. Water covered N Grand north of NW Windus St. NE Morton St by Reaney pool was flooded across all lanes. Grand Avenue closed from Nye to Ritchie. Main Street from Spring to Pine was closed. Morton Street near Reaney Park closed due to flooding.
Stalled vehicles at US Highway 90 and Debuys Road between Biloxi and Gulfport.
Fat Dragon Chinese Kitchen and Bar was closed due to flooding inside the building.
A few inches of water was reported in the lowest level of a home.
Flash flooding resulted in water inside a home.
Video shows a home flooded with ankle deep water.

A rapid water surge caused flooding across PR-936 in Quebrada Honda, overtopping a bridge and rendering the roadway impassable. A vehicle was swept from the roadway by the floodwaters while attempting to cross the bridge. Local emergency management personnel rescued the occupant, and no injuries were reported. The road remained closed after the event due to continued hazardous flooding conditions.
properties.epi: An amplifying mid- to upper-level trough, combined with above-normal moisture, maintained an unstable, wet pattern. With previous rain left saturated soils and elevated rivers, heavy rainfall quickly lead to urban flooding, small stream flooding, river flooding, landslides and flash flooding. Significant flooding occurred in Las Piedras, particularly, where several houses where flooded and flash flooded following heavy rainfall.

properties.note: One vehicle became stranded in a flooded underpass near the OH-430 and US-42 split east of downtown Mansfield. Several residences experienced flooding with several barricades placed due to street flooding. Radar estimated 1 to 1.75 inches of rainfall in one hour, with 0.5 to 0.8 inches in a 15 minute period, with equates to a 5 to 15 year average recurrence interval.
A social media video showed multiple vehicles stalled in flood waters in the Keller/Watauga area.
Flash flooding was reported. Streets were closed. Vehicles were stranded.
Due to flash flooding, vehicles became stuck on Route 35.
Flash flooding was reported north of the Walt Whitman Bridge. Roads were close. Vehicles were submerged.
Flash flooding was reported near the Ben Franklin Bridge. Roads were closed. Vehicles were submerged.
Flash flooding was reported. Roads were closed. Vehicles were submerged.
Multiple water rescues were reported in the city of Wilmington, including on Pennsylvania Ave, Bancroft Parkway, MLK Blvd, South Monroe Street, East 12th Street, and Dure Street.
Portions of Route 72 in Stafford Twp became impassable due to flash flooding. Some vehicles were disabled as a result.
Water rescues were needed on North Market St. Water was up to the doors of businesses with subjects stranded.
Water rescues were reported on Paper Mill and Creek View Rd.

Heavy rain caused flooding in the Lawrenceburg area. Geri Street was covered with water. Some water made it into the front door of a restaurant on the corner of Geri Street and Business Avenue. A driveway to a residence off of Buffalo Road near David Street was also washed out. Damages are a rough estimate.
An NWS employee reported flash flooding near the intersection of Highway 183 and Mockingbird Ln. Multiple high water rescue calls were made across Dallas.
Vehicle stranded in flood water with driver trapped inside. Road washed out due to flooding. Water up to knee height. No injury reported.
Basement collapse due to considerable flash flooding on West 20th Street.
Water entered the first floor of an apartment complex off of Darien Hwy in Brunswick, GA.
A video was sent in of cars stuck in high water on Route 35 in Ocean Township.
Swift water rescues were needed on Brush Fork Road for people trapped upstairs in their home.

Multiple mPing reports were received, spanning from the north Freeway around Independence Heights to the Sugarland area. Four indicated street flooding with vehicles stranded. One indicated a building had been inundated with water. Additionally, a storm chaser shared a video on social media showing water over the North Freeway frontage Road at West Rocky Creek Road. In the video, one vehicle appears to be stalled out, though others can be seen passing through.

Public report of JBS Pkwy flooded between Pearl and Trunk streets in Odessa with cars stalled out. The total time of occurrence is partially estimated from radar. The cost of damages is also estimated.
Three feet of standing water was observed at the intersection of Suds Run Road and Chub Run Road. Four unoccupied vehicles were submerged in the 1500 block of Suds Run Road.

Persistent heavy rain fell across the island of Oahu. Water flooded a residence in Waialua and over a foot of water was reported on Farrington Highway. Flooding was also reported at Waialua High and Intermediate School, and Komo St and Waialua Beach Rd, Waialua.

Flash flooding of streets and sidewalks mainly in northwest Milwaukee County, including stranded vehicles in floodwaters. Some reports of basement flooding in northern Milwaukee County. Pictures and videos provided.
Flash flooding of streets in Watertown. A few stranded vehicles across the city. A 3 to 4 foot sinkhole occurred due to the floodwaters.
High water was reported inside of multiple apartments near the Villages of Roll Hill.
Approximately eight homes near the intersection of Little York Road and Alvira Avenue in Butler Township had high water that intruded into the first floor.
Local broadcast media relayed a picture of stalled vehicles at the South Acadian underpass at I-10.
Local news showed the ground floor apartments at the end of Ida Street were inundated with flood waters.

US 271 was closed due to flooding just north of Pattonville. Multiple other roads were flooded and closed across Lamar County, including US Hwy 82 E from Sun Valley through Blossom, FM 79 to FM 2820, and FM 1499 from Us Hwy 271 N to Caviness. Part of FM 1499 was washed out.

Emergency Management reported flash flooding in Andrews, particularly around the city lake. A few cars were reported stalled due to flood waters. The total time of occurrence is estimated from radar, and the cost of damages is estimated.

A social media post showed widespread flooding along Highway 44, just north of Cazzie Cothern Road. The home was completely surrounded by water at least a few feet deep. Several vehicles appear to be flooded.

The Hana Police Department reported a landslide on the Hana Highway. The roadway was |temporarily closed to remove rock and debris. A nearby resort in the Hana area also reported trees downed from landslides.
A culvert was washed out on McDonald Cemetary Road near M&M Drive.

Five vehicles reported stranded in floodwaters in Racine from the Racine Police Department. 30 service calls taken by the Racine PD related to the flooding, including flooded roadways, underpasses, and uncovered manholes. Many yards and basements flooded. Flooding impacts also affected communities just to the west of Racine.
Beals Run was out of its banks with several inches of moving water impacting the first floor of businesses and homes on Millville Avenue.
Multiple vehicles were stalled due to flooding in Frontenac.
Pecos Fire Department reported several cars were stranded at 14th and Cedar Street due to flash flooding. The total time of occurrence is estimated from radar. The cost of damages is also estimated.
Washouts on East Hill Rd. and Marsh Hill Rd. in Wolcott, VT.

An estimated 5 to 7 inches of rain in the Byrdstown area caused flash flooding. The Wolf River crested to 15.29 inches which is the second highest crest on record going back to 1944. This flooding forced the closure of Burntmill Ford Road and S Ford Road where they cross the river. One nearby home also reported being inundated with water. Damages are a rough estimate for the home.

Social and broadcast media showed flooded streets and fast flowing water at least 6 to 12 inches deep in the Germantown area of Philadelphia. Several cars were floating in the water. Basements were flooded.

Significant street flooding occurred in the city of West Plains. Numerous streets were closed due to flooding. A home was flooded, a vehicle was submerged and extensive flooding occurred at a Dollar General store.
Multiple homes were flooded and vehicles were stranded due to flooding at State Highway 43 and Five Mile Creek.
Water was completely covering multiple roadways.
Several roads, including South Main, were closed due to flooding. A business was flooded, and the water covered a car up to its roof.
Between 6 and 8 inches of flood water entered an apartment complex on Exchange street in Ash Grove. The parking lot was flooded and nearly inaccessible.
Flooded roads across the county. Total rainfall for the event was around 3 inches.

Heavy rainfall within the Owasco Lake Inlet basin caused a rapid response and major flooding at the streamgage near Moravia. The inlet crested at 10.28 feet early in the morning of April 1st. The Major flood stage is 9.5 feet.
Heavy rain washed out a culvert and a portion of West County Road was washed out.

Due to the persistent heavy rain that fell over Oahu, widespread flooding over the east side of Oahu was observed on March 12 through March 13. Kapaa Quary Rd was closed on March 12. The next day a landslide was reported at Kapaa Quarry Rd and Kalanianaole Highway. Additionally on March 13, flooding was reported on Humupaa Pl. Emergency management reported a landslide on Auloa Rd 400 yards from Pali Hwy. Flooding was also observed on Kamehameha Highway, and near Hihimanu St and Waikupanaha Street.
Officials reported numerous roads flooded throughout the Town of Lansing along with some homes.
Reports of several cars stalled due to flooding near the intersection of West Esplanade and Loyola.

Extreme thunderstorm rainfall from slow-moving cells produced flash flooding in Fountain County south of Interstate 74, that stranded vehicles at the intersection of US Highways 136 and 41 and required high water rescues.
Sellers creek was out of it banks and homes were evacuated. Several roads around Mendenhall were covered with water.
Extreme thunderstorm rainfall up to 5.00-6.00 inches in under 4 hours near Linton and Switz City resulted in flash flooding that washed out a culvert on County Road 1225 West.
Picture on social media showed water in cars parked along Brownswitch Road in Slidell.
Broadcast media reporting video of stalled vehicles on US Highway 90 in Biloxi.
A high-water rescue occurred at the Black Bear Creek crossing amidst a period of prolonged flooding. The event time is estimated based on information from first responders.

Multiple sources confirmed widespread roadway flooding occurred in and near the outlined event area. This included several high-water rescues, road closures and erosion/damage in at least one location. The event time is approximate.
Multiple images showing large sections of 19th Avenue, between Underwood Road and Greenwood Road, eroded or collapsed due to flooding were shared on social media. The event time is approximate.
Heavy rain washed out a culvert and damaged Green Acres Road near Elsah.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. Part of FM 1376 at Wasp Creek was washed out by flood water.
Social media video showed rushing water across Camp Bowie Blvd in Fort Worth, with multiple vehicles stranded.
Social media video showed cars partially submerged on Hulen Street near Interstate 30 in the west part of Fort Worth, with water levels above the headlights.
A creek behind an animal shelter overflowed its banks, and flooded the building with a couple of feet of water.
Emergency management reported significant urban flash flooding with pictures of water 18 to 24 inches deep running down city streets.

Emergency management and local fire reported that multiple county and FM roads were flooded on Saturday, with several sustaining damage. Roads include CRs 132, 119, 120, 213, and 273 as well as FM 2027, 2269, 437, 1915, and 485.

Amateur radio reported that a garage and sunroom were flooded at a residence in Hewitt, near the intersection of Monterrey Drive and Alamosa. Water also leaked into the living room. 5.46 inches of rain was also reported in the area.

Extreme thunderstorm rainfall from slow-moving cells produced flash flooding across several counties near and west of Covington.|Flood waters were 3.0 feet deep with water 2.0 feet deep in home crawl spaces near the intersection of 1000 West and 950 South in Warren County, with locals noting the worst flooding in 20-30 years.
Road is completely washed out and not passable.
Vehicles stuck in flood waters along DuPont Highway.
Vehicles were stranded in flood waters on New Castle Ave.
CR 10W between CR 10S and CR 30S is completely washed out and not passable.
Reports from the local Fire Dept stated numerous roads in Hammonton were flooded, including Bellevue Avenue and 12th Street. Numerous cars were in flood waters all over town.
Heavy rain caused the parking lot of the Brentwood YMCA along with cars in the parking lot to become flooded, likely as the nearby creek overfilled its banks. Damages are a rough estimate.
A towing company reported numerous roads were flooded and impassable across northern Leon County.
Flash flooding was reported and resulted in numerous stranded cars. Water was two feet deep in spots.
Reports of flash flooding on Reeceville Road with multiple homes inundated.
Ten residences on the 100 block of Washington Court in Quakertown Borough were evacuated due to basement flooding.
Homes were filled with water.
Numerous roads were flooded around Paris including Northeast Loop 286 at Main Street, Lamar Avenue, and Deshong Drive. Several cars were stalled in the flood waters.
A trained spotter reported family living in Livingston Manor evacuated their home due to flooding.
Many intersections in Terre Haute are flooded with numerous reports of vehicles stranded in water.
A picture was sent in of water inside of the Jersey Shore Medical Center.
Photos showed several vehicles flooded in approximately 2 feet of water along Memorial Drive and 9th and 10th Avenues in Asbury Park. Roads were impassible.

To the southwest of Cody, heavy rain brought a flash flood and mudslide that severely damaged a bridge along Hunter Creek Road along the South Fork of the Shoshoni River over Boulder Creek. Three mudslides were also reported, some of them more than 6 feet deep. Several landowners near the Boulder Creek were stranded until a temporary bridge was installed.
Widespread flooding occurring on roadways throughout Wamego.
Flash flooding caused two swift water rescues in Columbia with three individuals rescued in total. No injuries were reported.
A culvert and part of a bridge were washed out, making the roadway impassable.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding on Creasy Springs Road where a water rescue took place. Elsewhere, a vehicle stalled in flood waters. The fire department had to rescue the occupant by boat.

Emergency management reported several high water calls at Interstate 30 underpasses, including the Hulen, Alta Mere, and Horne intersections. Social media video showed cars partially submerged on Hulen Street near Interstate 30 in the west part of Fort Worth, with water levels above the headlights.

Sand Run near Buckhannon exceeded a bankfull level of 6 feet on the evening of July 21st. The creek reached a crest of around 12.6 feet overnight and then receded below bankfull the next morning. Impacts from the river spilling out of its banks included flooding of low areas and outbuildings next to Sand Run, as well as some homes and roads near Sand Run.
The intersection of Highway 80 and Highway 35 in Forest was under water. Two cars were stranded.

An area of training showers and thunderstorms crossed portions of east central and northeastern Rutland County during the early morning hours of June 15. Rainfall reports of between 2 and 3.5 inches were received, most notably just east of Rutland along the Route 4 corridor. The Vermont Dept. of Highways reported several secondary roads having high water and being impassable due to flash flooding in this area.

The NWS River Watch team reported that extensive, high-impact overbank flooding occurred near Holy Cross because of the massive ice blockages downriver. The local airport runway was completely submerged and rendered entirely inoperable. Numerous lower-town structures were surrounded by water, and water entered several homes. Though the primary jam released on Friday (May 22), substantial stranded water kept the runway closed for days.

A social media post shows significant structure flooding at Lupulele Elementary School. Water covered the bottom floor of the building. Rainfall is estimated at 3 inches between 12 PM and 2 PM on May 18th. Monetary damage is estimated.
Trace Fork flooded Left Fork Scarlett Road, Gillman Drive, Midnight Lane, and Daystar Road. Residents were trapped and bridges were washed out.
The fire department relayed that a house was flooded with children reportedly trapped in Lott.
Flash flooding occurred with heavy rainfall on the 22nd over the Custer Motorway near Mill Creek. The Motorway was closed due to some rain caused mudslides causing some washouts.

Flash flooding from heavy rain impacted Aztec Park between N. Ash St. and Main St., as well as a Chevrolet Dealership along West Chaco Street. Emergency management reported water reaching about 1 foot infiltrated the dealership. Damage is an estimate.

A delayed report was received from a storm chaser, with photos showing cars submerged by flood waters in Hobbs. The time of occurrence is estimated from radar, and the cost of damages is also estimated.

Social media posts show flash flooding from heavy rainfall during the afternoon of the 18th in Fagaima village. Due to recent estate development and poor storm water drainage, multiple homes were flooded and village roadways were impassible. Monetary damage is estimated.
A bridge over a small creek north of Enterprise was pushed up and damaged by flooding.
Ice jam flooding occurred along the Allegheny River from Lock 9 to Lock 8. This impacted a campground on the right descending bank and also camps and homes on the left descending bank.
properties.epi: After a prolonged cold period that allowed for rapid river ice growth, a period of unusual warm temperatures helped to melt and rot the ice. During the melt process, some ice jams were observed along the Allegheny River and other tributaries along the Beaver and Ohio Rivers.

properties.note: A social media video showed numerous vehicles stalled in flood waters on Manana Dr at I-35E in Dallas.
properties.epi: Late on the night of June 18, coverage of showers and thunderstorms expanded in association with a cold front and a slow-moving shortwave trough. This system then pushed south through North Texas early the morning of June 19. As the front continued southward and the shortwave propagated eastward, a second round of showers and storms developed across Central Texas on Saturday, June 20. The primary hazard accompanying these storms was flash flooding, though a few instances of damaging winds were also reported.

properties.note: A social media video showed several vehicles stalled in flood waters on West Crosby Rd near I-35E in Dallas.

properties.epi: A couple rounds of showers and thunderstorms developed across portions of northeastern Oklahoma during the morning and afternoon of the 6th, as an upper level disturbance approached the region. Locally heavy rainfall from this activity resulted in some flash flooding in Creek, Tulsa, and Okmulgee Counties.

properties.note: A public report indicated significant underpass flooding at Harry Hines and Spur 482, with cars submerged up to the windshield. Additionally, all intersections along Northwest Highway near Bachman Lake were flooded and closed.

This system then pushed south through North Texas early the morning of June 19. As the front continued southward and the shortwave propagated eastward, a second round of showers and storms developed across Central Texas on Saturday, June 20. properties.note: The NWS River Watch team reported that heavy river ice jammed and backed up directly into the Andreafsky River near Saint Mary's, forcing it to flow backward upstream. Water levels rose significantly, causing damage to low-lying fish camps and smokehouses. Observers reported this as the highest water seen since the historic 1989 breakup.
properties.epi: As the third week of May 2026 unfolded, the dynamic breakup front stalled repeatedly along the Lower Yukon, creating a cascading sequence of severe jams and flooding. This period involved massive downstream surges as well as backwater effects in tributaries like the Andreafsky and Chuilnuk.

properties.note: Heavy rain of up to 7 inches resulted in street flooding due to persistent rainfall. Cars were reportedly stalled all over town.
properties.epi: A thunderstorm complex moved south through Illinois during the day of May 18th. Isolated wind damage occurred in Montgomery County, and isolated flooding occurred in Marion County.

properties.note: Multiple sources reported significant flash flooding developed across northeast Henderson County after 4 to 7 inches of rain fell on the slopes of Bearwallow Mountain in just a couple of hours. The main impact was to Clear Creek and its tributaries, including Puncheon Camp Creek, Cox Creek, and Laurel Fork. A culvert washed out underneath a section of Highway 74 in the Gerton community, forcing closure of the road for a few days. A section of Bearwallow Rd was also washed out in the Edneyville area. Multiple other roads were inundated and closed throughout the area, while multiple culverts…
properties.epi: Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed across western North Carolina during the afternoon and evening. A series of thunderstorm cells became anchored on the slopes of Bearwallow Mountain in Henderson County, resulting in torrential rainfall that lasted for a couple of hours, resulting in flash flooding.

properties.note: Heavy rain flooded a house. Sandbags were provided due to the rising water. Total rainfall for the event was around 3 inches.
properties.epi: During the 18th midday and afternoon hours, a fast-moving line of severe thunderstorms swept through central Indiana, producing widespread damaging straight line winds. The severe weather entered the western portions of the IND CWA shortly after 1200 EST, with initial damage reported in Parke and Clay Counties where multiple trees and three power poles were downed. The line tracked quickly eastward through the early afternoon, impacting the Indianapolis metropolitan area and adjacent counties. Widespread wind damage to trees and utility lines was noted, particularly across Owen County where an estimated gust of 55 knots (63 mph) downed a significant number of trees and powerlines. Further north, an estimated 60 mph gust in Boone County was followed by a measured gust of 53 knots (61 mph) at the Indianapolis Executive Airport north of Zionsville at 1335 EST. Power lines were also downed…

properties.note: Heavy rain led to road closures between Naalehu and Pahala due to a culvert overflowing. Highway 11 was also closed at Kawa Flats due to flooding. Then on March 14, water over Highway 11 cut off the towns on Naalehu and Pahala. The Department of Transportation reported Hawaii Belt Road (Route 11) at mile marker 57.5 at the Hilea Stream Bridge was closed due to flooding in the area.
properties.epi: From March 12th through March 14th of 2026, a large and powerful kona storm setup over the northern central Pacific, and brought numerous impacts across the state. This low was supported by a broad and potent upper level trough that lingered for many days. Impacts included flash flooding, wind damage, large surf, and strong thunderstorms.

properties.note: Early in the morning of March 22nd, heavy rain moved over Maui and led to flooding across the island. Many roads were flooded and landslides were reported. Keawe St. was closed in both directions between Kupuohi St. and Kuhua St. due to flooding. Both lanes of Honoapiilani Highway were blocked near mile marker 33 due to a landslide. Kahekili Highway was closed from 2120 Kahekili Highway to Kahakuloa due to flooding. Kapunakea St. and Front St. intersection was closed due to flooding. Kahekili Highway was closed from 2120 Kahekili Hwy to Kahakuloa due to flooding. Hana Highway/Hanakai St. to…
properties.epi: A cutoff low moved in from the northwest and pulled deep tropical moisture from the south over the Hawaiian islands. This led to the development of prolonged slow moving heavy rain and thunderstorms. The heavy rain and thunderstorms caused catastrophic flooding over Oahu's North Shore and Manoa Valley.

properties.note: Heavy rain moved over southern Oahu in Honolulu and east Honolulu from the south. Flooding was reported on Queen Street and Kapiolani Boulevard. Landslides were reported on Diamond Head Road, the Punchbowl ramp onto the H1 west bound, and the Pali Highway ramp onto the H1 east bound. Flooding occurred on the H1 Pali offramp, and on Kalanianaole Highway. Significant erosion and undermining of Kalanianaole Highway caused total closure of the highway in both directions near Sealife Park. Nine homeless people and dog were rescued in the Manoa-Palolo Stream near Kaimuki High School due to rapidly…

This low was supported by a broad and potent upper level trough that lingered for many days. Impacts included flash flooding, wind damage, large surf, and strong thunderstorms.

properties.note: Extreme thunderstorm rainfall from slow-moving cells produced flash flooding along Indiana Route 28 and into multiple homes west of West Lebanon. The Redwood Creek river gage at Route 28, RCMI3, rose from 4.79 to 13.43 feet in 1.5 hours to 1945 EST.
properties.epi: On the 6th afternoon to early evening, a moist column combined with dynamic lift from an approaching cool front to produce numerous to widespread training thunderstorms over northern portions of central Indiana. While most cells were generally sub-severe, isolated damaging winds were most organized in Warren County and most intense at the Muncie airport. More noteworthy was the quasi-parallel nature of the approaching boundary to the moist conveyor's axis, which produced multiple roudns of heavy rain over several zones, and considerable flash flooding in portions of Warren County and Fountain County where up to an estimated 7.00 inches of rain fell. This severe weather event would be the first of many for the month which would eventually define a formal disaster period from June 6th to the 18th which was declared by the governor of Indiana.

properties.note: Three feet of water was over Highway 49 in the Seminary area. Some vehicles were trapped in flood waters.
properties.epi: Additional heavy rainfall along with wet antecedent conditions lead to more flash flooding, some significant, in the Pine Belt region of Mississippi. Several major roads were flooded, as well as homes. Water rescues were conducted in the Seminary area as several cars became stranded.

properties.note: Video of homes flooding in the Bayou Cane area.
properties.epi: A mesoscale convective system formed on the eastern side of Post-Tropical Storm Arthur on June 18th. Favorable low level winds allowed for multiple mini-supercells to form on the leading edge of the mesoscale convective system resulting in several tornadoes impacting the Houma and New Orleans metro areas. These tornadoes were rated as EF-0 and EF-1 events. Additionally, the mesoscale convective complex tapped into a region of deep tropical moisture with atmospheric moisture content well above normal levels for mid-June. This resulted in several significant flash flooding events in portions of the Houma and New Orleans metro areas including the cities of Houma, Kenner, and Slidell. Another area of heavy rainfall from thunderstorms formed over central Louisiana near the center of Post-Tropical Storm Arthur producing flash flooding in portions of Pointe Coupee Parish. Lingering moisture…

properties.note: Emergency managers reported flooding along Calle Mirtos in Valle Hermoso Arriba, Hormigueros. They stated that a sewer overflowed, causing problems at one house where water entered the first floor. Based on radar estimates, around 2 inches of rain fell.
properties.epi: On the afternoon of April 30th, locally induced showers with isolated thunderstorms developed over portions of the interior and north-central PR and steered by southeasterly winds towards the western half. This resulted in urban and small stream flooding, as well as isolated flash flooding, over sectors of interior to western PR including Hormigueros through the evening hours.

properties.note: Flash flooding occurred along Bear and Upper Bear Creek in the Evergreen/Kittridge area late evening June 24 2006 and early morning June 25. Rainfall reports showed two to four inches of rain fell in a two hour period with much of it falling in one hour. Damage occurred to businesses and home along Bear Creek in the Evergreen/Kittridge area.
properties.epi: Numerous thunderstorms tracked across eastern Colorado during the late afternoon and evening hours of the 24th. Hail, strong winds, and two tornadoes were observed. In addition heavy rainfall in the Evergreen area produced flash flooding late on the 24th and early on the 25th.

properties.note: Emergency management reported that several county roads were flooded and some sustained culvert damage or failures, including County Roads 1495, 1325, 3425, 2350, and 1150. Additionally, a section of County Road 2300 was flooded due to a small private earthen dam being overtopped due to the locally heavy rain.
properties.epi: From April 24 to April 27, daily thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon and evening, triggered by a dryline and a meandering frontal boundary. These long-lasting supercells were fueled by a highly unstable and sheared environment, resulting in several tornadoes, damaging winds, and very large hail. Two fatalities occurred on April 25th.

properties.note: Significant flash flooding occurred across North Richland Hills after several inches of rain fell in a short amount of time. A few notable reports were: Cars were stuck in high water along Bedford Euless Road; other high water rescues were reported around the city; Calloway Creek overflowed flooding nearby areas; water was approaching homes, including on Odell St, and sand bags were requested to keep the water away from homes.
properties.epi: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed on a daily basis across the region over Memorial Day weekend as a result of several passing upper level disturbances. Some storms produced severe hail, damaging winds, and flash flooding. Significant flash flooding occurred in North Richland Hills in Tarrant County on May 25th.

properties.note: Heavy rainfall associated with thunderstorms developed over Oahu. This led to flash flooding and multiple roads were closed. Water flooded a residence in Royal Kunia. Flooding was reported on Farrington Highway in Waipahu, Kamehameha Highway near the Waikane Stream, and Waiahole Valley Road.
properties.epi: A cold upper level low approached the Hawaiian islands and led to thunderstorms and flooding.

properties.note: Social media images from the Prince George Police Department showed flooding in the Pine Ridge community, with water almost onto the hood of a sedan.
properties.epi: Slow-moving showers and storms resulted in locally heavy rainfall and localized flash flooding across central Virginia on May 26.

properties.note: Numerous Facebook reports indicated significant flooding across Athens with several cars submerged. Roads flooded and closed included Valle Vista Drive, FM 317, and streets around downtown Athens.
properties.epi: Over the course of the weekend, a meandering front and an unseasonably strong upper trough triggered widespread showers and thunderstorms across the region. Heavy rain from training storms ultimately resulted in flash flooding, particularly affecting several Central Texas counties. A significant flood event occurred in and around Waco costing millions of dollars.

properties.note: Broadcast media reported significant urban flash flooding near the intersection of Waco Drive and Lake Air Drive in Waco. Multiple cars were seen stranded in the photo, which was relayed from social media. Local Emergency Management reported approximately 60 persons were rescued or needed assistance to safety across the county.

properties.note: Flash flooding was reported into the town of Junction off the Cottonwood burn scar. Media reports that the flash flood broke through a berm built to divert flood waters, inundating portions of the town. Time estimated. Additionally, flash flooding from Cottonwood burn scar sent debris flowing over US-89 between mile markers 164 and 177.
properties.epi: A monsoonal pattern persisted onward through mid July, resulting in more instances of thunderstorm winds and flash flooding.

properties.note: The Dona Ana County Flood Commission reported flooding along Ranch Road and Cox Farm Road. An unmaintained berm failed upstream of the mesa causing flash flooding of a property along Ranch Road. There was also widespread cleanup of water in homes in Chamberino. An unmaintained earthen dam failed upstream, causing flash flooding in town.
properties.epi: Moisture lingered over southern New Mexico as an upper high became situated over Colorado. A weak upper trough moved through Texas and helped to support slow moving thunderstorms with heavy rain and some severe wind gusts over Dona Ana and Grant counties.

properties.note: Schertz ordered mandatory evacuations for all residents of the Pecan Grove RV Park and voluntary evacuations for Lone Oak, Rio Vista, Buffalo Valley South, and areas along southern FM 78 and FM 1518 to Lisa Meadows, followed by the 200-300 block of Aviation Heights. Several roads were closed in the Schertz area along Cibolo Creek. An RV was observed stranded along Aztec Way, apparently moved and damaged by floodwaters. A water rescue was reported at 6:30 PM CST on West Schaefer Rd. in Cibolo on July 17.
properties.epi: A strong upper-level ridge moved over the northern Great Plains allowing a moist, tropical airmass to move over South-Central Texas. Precipitable water values increased to greater than 2.0 inches which were near or above the 95th percentile of climatological values for this part of July. Multiple rounds of excessive rainfall were triggered by mid-level disturbances around the southern periphery of the high and low-level outflow boundaries. This convection was aided by nocturnal low-level jet streaks which led to slow moving, back building thunderstorms. Most of South-Central Texas received more than two inches of rain. The greatest totals were over Uvalde and Kinney Counties where 20-30 inches occurred. Another local maximum of 15-20 inches was observed in central Kerr County. Ten to 15 inches were widespread from Del Rio to Hondo and northward to northeastern Edwards to western…

properties.note: An ice jam on the Koyukuk River near Hughes impounded a significant volume of water. This caused water levels to submerge properties in the lower sections of the community, directly impacting local residences, school property, and the airport. Local residents and members of the Alaska State EOC indicated that the ice set up late Friday night and then released Saturday afternoon. However, a secondary jam set up soon after which was responsible for sending most of the water into the community. Numerous families were sheltered at the local community hall which is located on higher ground.
properties.epi: The 2026 spring breakup along the Yukon River was highly dynamic, defined by a combination of thermal ice decay and severe mechanical ice jams. Because of an exceptionally cold winter and a cool spring, the river ice was thicker than normal and had not deteriorated significantly before the main breakup front arrived. Early-season flooding was driven by localized snowmelt and ice jams on independent river systems and upper sections of the Yukon River.

properties.note: Four families near Lettsworth had to be evacuated from their homes after water entered their home. Water depth reached to about 8 inches inside of the homes.

properties.note: The Buckhannon River near Buckhannon exceeded a flood stage of 23 feet on the night of July 21st. The river then rose to a crest of around 27.6 feet on the morning of the 22nd before falling back below flood stage that evening. Major flooding was observed in Buckhannon and surrounding areas as a result. Six feet of water near Weyerhaeuser was measured during this time, a car that floated down East Main Street, a submerged vehicle was observed near Lumber Street, and a home was impacted by flooding on Wimer Avenue. A water rescue occurred on 5th Street while a car was also submerged in water…
properties.epi: An upper level trough descended into the northeast quadrant of the United States while a surface low ambled east across Ontario and Quebec. The system first lifted a warm front through the middle Ohio Valley and Central Appalachians on the night of July 20th into the early morning of the 21st, then steered a cold front east across the area late that evening into the night.||Showers and thunderstorms began to develop by late morning on the 21st, with a broken line of stronger storms progressing across the area during the afternoon and evening. Severe thunderstorms produced two main swaths of damage across the area. The first swath of damage encompassed areas along and north of a line from Wood County east to Randolph County, while the second was primarily concentrated along and near the I-64 corridor. In addition to numerous reports of downed trees and power outages, some notable areas…

properties.note: The NWS River Watch team flying the Lower Yukon reported an ice jam forming roughly 8 miles downstream of Marshall caused the Yukon River to back up rapidly into the main town, adjacent sloughs, tributaries, and wetlands. Water levels finally began a slow recession of up to one foot on Saturday, May 23.

properties.note: The NWS River Watch team observed a 30-mile thick run of bank to bank ice pushing towards the coast that caused Kwiguk Pass to jam up heavily at it's mouth, backing floodwaters directly into the village of Emmonak. The river stage surged to 9.7 feet (approaching the historic 11.5-foot record), leaving all roads to the local airport entirely impassable by vehicles. The Emmonak High School had to be opened as an emergency shelter for displaced residents.
properties.epi: The dynamic breakup front finally arrived at the lower reaches of the Yukon River across the Yukon Delta by late May 2026. This resulted in severe, cascading flood impacts for multiple communities as the high water made it's way to the mouth of the Yukon River, inundating the coastal delta.

properties.note: Several roads were washed out, with around 8 feet of water.
properties.epi: Severe storms with sufficient shear and instability produced severe weather across central Mississippi. The main feature, a mesovortex within a broken line of storms, produced several weak, brief tornadoes and some damaging winds in central Mississippi. This event featured multiple rounds of storms as well as heavy rainfall, which led to flash flooding across southeastern portions of the area.

properties.note: Flooded roads across the county. Total rainfall for the event was around 2 inches.

properties.note: Heavy rains washed out a bridge on County Road 1100 North at Wolf Creek.
properties.epi: Between the evening of March 3 and the late hours of March 4, 2026, a significant hydrologic event unfolded across central Indiana as a stalled frontal boundary interacted with a highly anomalous moisture profile. Driven by a robust 50-knot low-level jet, precipitable water values surged to nearly 1.30 inches���well above the 90th percentile for early March. While the Storm Prediction Center initially identified a low-probability severe threat, the environment was dominated by deep-layer moisture transport and training convective elements, leading to widespread 48-hour rainfall totals of 4 to 6 inches.

properties.note: Extreme thunderstorm rainfall up to 5.00-6.00 inches in under 4 hours from east of Sullivan to south of Bloomfield, produced flash flooding in Linton, Lyons and Switz City. In Linton, vehicles stalled out, a child swept away by water was rescued, and railroad ties floated through town. Additionally, a culvert was washed out in Greene County on County Road 475 West, while Indiana Route 54 was flooded out in Sullivan County east of Sullivan.
properties.epi: On the 27th afternoon to early evening, a stationary west-east frontal boundary combined with a very moist column and forcing from a short wave trough over the Middle Mississippi Valley, to produce heavy to extreme rainfall rates over Sullivan and Greene Counties, and later Martin County. Resultant flash flooding was considerable during the afternoon east of Sullivan through the Linton area. Less impactful early evening flash flooding occurred in Martin County.

properties.note: Multiple sources confirmed significant and widespread flash flooding on the morning of June 23rd in and near the outlined event area. This included numerous roadways that were significantly flooded, with several high-water rescues reported, including along U.S. Highway 69/75. Some roadways were also washed out or collapsed. This flooding resulted in the issuance of a rare Flash Flood Emergency, the first across the WFO Norman Forecast Area since May of 2019. The event time is approximate.
properties.epi: An active severe weather and flooding event impacted the WFO Norman Forecast Area form the morning into early evening of the 23rd. An initial complex of severe thunderstorms moved from northwestern into southwestern Oklahoma and eventually western-north Texas during this time, producing reports of large hail and observations of severe winds. A separate complex of slow-moving thunderstorms entered southeastern Oklahoma during the mid-morning, fostered by ascent atop a strong outflow boundary. Slow storm movement and rich boundary layer moisture combined to yield significant flash flooding across portions of Atoka County, Oklahoma. Eventually, these two separate areas of thunderstorms merged across central Oklahoma, yielding additional severe weather (mainly damaging winds) and flooding during the afternoon and early evening hours.

properties.note: A portion of County Route 2 was washed out due to flood waters just west of South Schodack Road in the Town of Schodack.
properties.epi: An unprecedented heavy rain event/rain storm impacted eastern NY and western New England on July 28-30, 2026. Scattered to numerous instances of flash flooding occurred with the Greater Capital Region, eastern Catskills and northern portions of the mid-Hudson Valley being the hardest hit. A closed/cutoff low was positioned over the region. The mid and upper low captured a double-barrel low pressure system with one low centered over eastern/southern NY and a secondary coastal low southeast of Long Island. Meso-vortices migrated around the mid and upper level low over the region. A tremendous fetch of deep moisture occurred from the Atlantic and Gulf. Precipitable water anomalies were 2-3 standard deviations above normal in the 1.40-1.80 inch range. Freezing levels were high in the 11-13 kft above ground level range. Very efficient rainfall processes occurred with more of a cool season…

properties.note: Bone Creek caused extensive flooding of several homes along Main Street, with up to 3 feet of water reported in some of the homes.

properties.note: The collision of two outflow boundaries right over Amarillo created additional thunderstorms that produced efficient rainfall of likely two to three inch per hour rainfall rates. These storms did not move out of the area quickly and heavy rainfall resulted in widespread flash flooding, especially across portions of the southwest side of the city. Fast moving flood waters occurred across many streets and parking lots, some of which were anywhere from six to eight inches deep or even up to 12 inches deep. There were multiple to numerous impassable roads with swift flowing water across them and…
properties.epi: Moisture was high for mid July across the combined Panhandles with precipitable water values in the 90th percentile. This would result in efficient rainfall occurring from any storm that developed during the afternoon and evening hours of July 12th. A weak upper level disturbance moved across the region, and coupled with heating and unstable atmosphere, was able to produce some showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon. Outflow boundaries also contributed to additional storm development, including one that formed across the city of Amarillo and persisted for a long time. This storm produced efficient heavy rainfall that resulted in significant flooding across downtown and the southern sections of the city. Additionally, damaging winds and even a landspout occurred during these storms.

properties.note: Emergency management reported that multiple people were stranded near the intersection of 60th and Sanger in Waco. During this event, Waco reported 73 vehicles involved in water incidents and at least 6 structures flooded.

properties.note: Portions of several county roads were washed out between Bristow and Kellyville.
properties.epi: A couple rounds of showers and thunderstorms developed across portions of northeastern Oklahoma during the morning and afternoon of the 6th, as an upper level disturbance approached the region. Locally heavy rainfall from this activity resulted in some flash flooding in Creek, Tulsa, and Okmulgee Counties.

properties.note: The NWS River Watch team observed severe, high-impact flooding at Pilot Station due to an ice jam. A river gauge registered a sudden 5-foot rise in a single day, eventually peaking at 33.76 feet on Sunday afternoon. All local roads became completely impassable except by boat, and multiple homes were impacted. Floodwaters officially exceeded 2024 levels, making this the worst flooding the community had seen since 1989.

properties.note: Heavy rain developed over the southeastern slopes of the Big Island and led to flooding impacts. Water was reportedly flowing into a house in the Puna district near Hawaiian Paradise Park. Water also accumulated on Highway 11 near mile marker 60. Hao Springs Road closed due to flooding.
properties.epi: An upper level trough and low level trough to the northwest of Hawaii brought numerous flooding impacts. These flooding impacts closed roads and damaged property across the state.

properties.note: The fire department reported multiple houses were flooding on Pecan Ave in Wills Point. Local FD requested a boat and were going door to door evacuating residents. Four to five feet of water was prohibiting egress on foot.
properties.epi: A slow-moving front and a handful of upper level disturbances brought multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms to North and Central Texas March 4 through 7, resulting in hail and flash flooding in some cases.

properties.note: The fire department reported knee deep water over Highway 80 near Big Tex Trailers at the Wills Point city limit. Wills Point Fire and Edgewood Fire were working multiple calls for flooding of stranded occupants in vehicles on Highway 80.
properties.epi: A slow-moving front and a handful of upper level disturbances brought multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms to North and Central Texas March 4 through 7, resulting in hail and flash flooding in some cases.

properties.note: Thunderstorm rainfall up to 6.00 inches caused widespread flash flooding across central and northern Daviess County, with at least 3 water rescues in Washington and at least 3 additional water rescues in other parts of the county from widespread inundated county roads, some with deep water flowing across; water additionally flowed into multiple homes. Flash flooding also impacted west-central Martin County where a CVS in Loogootee had water 2.5 feet deep at its lower back door, while water flowed over several roads north of Loogootee.
properties.epi: The 21st late day brought a quickly-evolving set-up featuring an increasingly moist column supported by an approaching Middle Mississippi Valley upper short wave trough, strengthening flow amid a warm frontal zone draped over the local central Indiana region providing 35-50KT of effective wind shear, and advection of higher low-level dewpoints with daytime heating which provided sufficient destabilization. Severe rotating supercells tracked across Illinois into southern central Indiana as they aligned into a Mesoscale Convective Vortex (MCV).||Wind damage occurred within nine central Indiana zones and as far east as Brown County, five (mainly EF-0) tornadoes were focused in Owen County and points south and west, while the region's farthest southwestern counties experienced scattered flash flooding following downpours from multiple supercells. A final EF-0 torando and flash flooding…

properties.note: Heavy rainfall led to multiple flooding impacts across the northern half of Oahu. Police reported to emergency management that Ke Nui Road just west of Ehukai Beach Park |was impassable due to flooding. Wilikina Dr was closed at Kaukonahua Rd due to flooding. Large boulders on Kamehameha Highway was closed the road in both directions.
properties.epi: An upper level trough and low level trough to the northwest of Hawaii brought numerous flooding impacts. These flooding impacts closed roads and damaged property across the state.

properties.note: Numerous high water rescues were conducted across Farmers Branch, including the I-35E entrance ramp at Valley View Rd, 3100 Brookhaven Club Dr, Josey Ln at Pyramid Dr, and Midway Rd at Spring Valley Rd.
properties.epi: Late on the night of June 18, coverage of showers and thunderstorms expanded in association with a cold front and a slow-moving shortwave trough. This system then pushed south through North Texas early the morning of June 19. As the front continued southward and the shortwave propagated eastward, a second round of showers and storms developed across Central Texas on Saturday, June 20. The primary hazard accompanying these storms was flash flooding, though a few instances of damaging winds were also reported.

properties.note: Numerous high water rescues were conducted across Carrollton, with locations including Sherwood Ln at Josey Ln, 1401 Dunn Dr, N Josey Ln at E Jackson Rd, Nix Rd at Fyke Rd, Hutton Dr at W Belt Line Rd, Bowie Dr at Nix Rd, and Mill Rd at Lockwood Dr.

properties.epi: A very moist and moderately unstable airmass was in place across southwest Mississippi during the morning of January 10th. Precipitable water values were around 1.7 inches, well above the climatological 90th percentile and near record for this time of year. A prefrontal convergence zone, enhanced by outflow boundaries and strong low-level moisture transport, supported a corridor of training showers and thunderstorms along the Louisiana/Mississippi border into southwest Mississippi. Within this environment, repeated rounds of heavy rainfall produced rain rates of 1 to 3 inches per hour. Training convection resulted in widespread rainfall totals of several inches with localized amounts approaching or exceeding a foot of rain across portions of Amite and Pike Counties over a relatively short period. This led to widespread flash flooding, including inundated roadways, stranded vehicles,…

properties.note: The combination of heavy rain and snow melt led to the West Canada Creek to overflow its banks from Hinckley Reservoir down to Kast Bridge and slightly farther downstream. Local news stations shared pictures and videos of flooding occurring in spots along the entire path of the creek from Poland to Newport and Middleville with water encroaching on river-adjacent homes, roadways, and local businesses.
properties.epi: The combination of persistent rounds of moderate to heavy rainfall; above-normal temperatures; and subsequent snowmelt led to several days worth of significant flooding along the West Canada Creek in Herkimer County.||The West Canada Creek USGS river gauge at Hinckley Reservoir reported minor flooding beginning around 9:45 PM EDT on March 31. The gauge then rose to moderate flood stage around 2:00 AM EDT on April 1. properties.note: The combination of heavy rain and snow melt led to the West Canada Creek to overflow its banks from Hinckley Reservoir down to Kast Bridge and slightly farther downstream. Local news stations shared pictures and videos of flooding occurring in spots along the entire path of the creek from Poland to Newport and Middleville with water encroaching on river-adjacent homes, roadways, and local businesses.

properties.note: Water entered Keith's Gas Station in Seminary. Two cars went into the ditch nearby. Local residents abandoned cars on roads, with water rescues conducted by the local fire department. Several homes were flooded as well.
properties.epi: Additional heavy rainfall along with wet antecedent conditions lead to more flash flooding, some significant, in the Pine Belt region of Mississippi. Several major roads were flooded, as well as homes. Water rescues were conducted in the Seminary area as several cars became stranded.

properties.note: Heavy rain developed over the eastern slopes of Maui. Emergency management and the local news reported multiple impacts. Hawaii News Now reported Hana High & Elementary School was temporarily closed on Tuesday April 7 due to flooding. The Department of Education said some classrooms had water damage. Water was also reported on Hana Highway.
properties.epi: An upper level trough and low level trough to the northwest of Hawaii brought numerous flooding impacts. These flooding impacts closed roads and damaged property across the state.

properties.note: Flooding led to a partial road washout along a portion of Millers Corners Road in the Town of Sand Lake.
properties.epi: An unprecedented heavy rain event/rain storm impacted eastern NY and western New England on July 28-30, 2026. Scattered to numerous instances of flash flooding occurred with the Greater Capital Region, eastern Catskills and northern portions of the mid-Hudson Valley being the hardest hit. A closed/cutoff low was positioned over the region. The mid and upper low captured a double-barrel low pressure system with one low centered over eastern/southern NY and a secondary coastal low southeast of Long Island. Meso-vortices migrated around the mid and upper level low over the region. A tremendous fetch of deep moisture occurred from the Atlantic and Gulf. Precipitable water anomalies were 2-3 standard deviations above normal in the 1.40-1.80 inch range. Freezing levels were high in the 11-13 kft above ground level range. Very efficient rainfall processes occurred with more of a cool season…

In addition, 23 adults, five children and six dogs were rescued at Schodack Island State Park due to flooding at the park entrance road along Route 9J.

properties.note: Vehicles were stranded in high water due to heavy rainfall from thunderstorms which dropped 1.2 to 2 inches of rainfall in about 30 minutes. There were two partially submerged vehicles at Sherman and Southeastern Ave while yard and basement flooding were also reported.
properties.epi: During the 27th afternoon and evening, a warm unstable air mass interacting with an upper wave and associated surface boundary developed scattered severe thunderstorms across central Indiana. Convection initiated around 15:27 EST over northern portions of central Indiana and overspread locations further south before diminishing during the evening hours.||Severe thunderstorm wind gusts were the primary hazard, with peak gusts estimated and measured between 58 mph and 60 mph. Official surface observations included a 58 mph gust recorded by the Muncie ASOS (KMIE) in Delaware County and a 59 mph gust at the Indianapolis ASOS (KIND) in Marion County. Wind damage was scattered across most eastern counties and a couple western zones, with numerous downed trees and powerlines, snapped utility poles and localized structural damage. Hail up to 1.25 inches in diameter was reported in Marion and…

properties.note: Numerous homes were flooded along the Warm Springs Creek with over a foot of water in some homes. Some cars were damaged. Ranches to the east and south of Thermopolis reported fences pulled out of the ground and stretched across the road. C Ave and Carter Ranch Road were flooded with moving water over them during the late evening and into the overnight hours.
properties.epi: Deep monsoonal moisture moved over Wyoming in the wake of the record heat wave. A strong thunderstorm developed to the east of Thermopolis and dropped approximately 4 inches of rain in an hour and a half. Warm Springs Creek overflowed and set a flash flood through ranches and into East Thermopolis.

properties.note: Emergency manager reported multiple main roads in Balch Springs were flooded with stranded motorists. Several houses had water of an unknown depth inside. Numerous side streets were also flooded.
properties.epi: A slow-moving front and a handful of upper level disturbances brought multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms to North and Central Texas March 4 through 7, resulting in hail and flash flooding in some cases.

properties.note: Several businesses in Picayune have been flooded from heavy rainfall.
properties.epi: A mesoscale convective system formed on the eastern side of Post-Tropical Storm Arthur on June 18th. Favorable low level winds allowed for multiple mini-supercells to form on the leading edge of the mesoscale convective system resulting in a few tornadoes affecting coastal Mississippi. These tornadoes were rated as EF-0 and EF-1 events. A bow echo also developed over coastal Mississippi leading to severe winds and thunderstorm wind damage in the Gulfport-Biloxi metro area. Additionally, the mesoscale convective complex tapped into a region of deep tropical moisture with atmospheric moisture content well above normal levels for mid-June. This resulted in several significant flash flooding events in portions of coastal Mississippi including the city of Picayune. Two fatalities occurred near Picayune where rainfall rates of 2 to 3 inches per hour and QPE of 10 to 15 inches was noted. This…

properties.note: Emergency management reported significant urban flash flooding along the 1400 block of Hewitt Drive in Waco.
properties.epi: Over the course of the weekend, a meandering front and an unseasonably strong upper trough triggered widespread showers and thunderstorms across the region. Heavy rain from training storms ultimately resulted in flash flooding, particularly affecting several Central Texas counties. A significant flood event occurred in and around Waco costing millions of dollars.

properties.note: Traffic cameras indicated that I-35 at Church Camp Lane in the south part of Waco was completely submerged in both directions and closed.

properties.note: The Vlockie Kill at Shufelt Road in the Town of Shodack flooded out of its banks, with water very close to the first floor of several nearby buildings. A portion of the road was also washed out.

properties.note: The public reported numerous basements flooded in the town of Le Roy with several vehicles submerged.
properties.epi: Repeated rounds of storms over portions of southeast Minnesota during the afternoon and evening hours on July 8th resulted in scattered instances of flash flooding during this timeframe. This included a closure of Interstate 90 due to flooding near Austin. The excessive rainfall also resulted in Dobbins Creek near Austin reaching into flood stage. Unrelated to flooding impacts, lightning from these storms struck a house in Winona which started a small fire.

properties.note: County emergency management reported that the M-69 bridge was closed on the 21st and advised residents to evacuate if they resided near flooded waters. On the 18th, social media reports showed inundation for low lying areas in the town of Amasa including damage to local parks and residential septic systems. Deer Lake became inaccessible due to road washouts on the 18th. Flooding in Sagola resulted in railroad washouts. Due to the severity of the flooding, a Disaster Declaration Request was approved by the president on June 30th.
properties.epi: Heavy rainfall and snowmelt resulted in flooding across the south-central U.P. Many roads were flooded and several closed. The flooding also caused damage at the Escanaba Airport (KESC) due to standing water on the runways and power failure. Due to the severity of the flooding, a Disaster Declaration Request was approved by the president on June 30th for Menominee and Marquette counties.

properties.note: Videos and reports of flash flooding along Hope Creek near Davenport Drive and Southampton Drive. Several homes with water intrusion into the first floors along with vehicles flooded. Damage cost is estimated.
properties.epi: A lingering stalled front remained in the forecast area 5/23, but a embedded shortwave in the general troughing pattern moved in during the afternoon and evening hours, leading to scattered convection to develop. The environment ahead of this shortwave was characterized by MLCAPE values over 2000 J/kg and effective shear near 30-35 kts. Scattered strong to severe storms moved across the forecast area during the afternoon and evening hours, bringing damaging winds, hail up to golf ball sized, and even a report of a waterspout over Lake Murray in SC.

properties.note: The Village of Holly issued a local state of emergency after flooding damaged pumps at its Waste Water Treatment Plant and impacted hundreds of homes. Water levels rose high enough to enter backyards and sheds. In some neighborhoods, residents reported water reaching the floorboards of their homes. The Road Commission for Oakland County (RCOC) was forced to close North Holly Road (just north of Quick Road near Holly Middle School) on the evening of April 4. The closure remained in place for several days due to standing water and road instability.
properties.epi: A cold front moved across Southeast Michigan during the late afternoon and early evening of April 4. This triggered two lines of thunderstorms that caused pockets of damage south of I-94. The most significant storm occurred in Wayne County, producing an EF-1 tornado in Van Buren Township. The system also dumped 1 to 3 inches of rain, with some areas seeing up to 4 inches. Because the region had already received 3 to 5 inches over the previous five days, these additional downpours caused the Tittabawassee, Clinton, and Flint rivers to overflow. In addition, significant localized flooding occurred on already saturated ground, with the hardest-hit area being northwest Oakland County, specifically in and around Holly.

properties.note: Flood waters from heavy rain over Avoyelles Parish drained southward through Saint Landry Parish. This inundated many roads between Highway 71 and the Atchafalaya Basin levee. Evacuations also occurred as residences were cut off. Some residences in northeast Saint Landry flooded during the event.
properties.epi: Tropical Storm Arthur made landfall along the coast of southeast Texas and moved northeast across central Louisiana. Heavy rain trained across portions of central Louisiana creating widespread flooding and a new rainfall record. Flood waters slowly drained in the days following the passage of the system.

properties.note: Very heavy rain produced flooding across large portions of Groves, Nederland, and Port Arthur. Many roads were flooded and impassable while numerous homes flooded.
properties.epi: A very moist airmass fueled slow moving storms in southeast Texas. Flooding was reported.

properties.note: Flooding affected at least 16 families in Las Piedras following heavy rainfall. One residence reported approximately 3 feet of water inside the home, resulting in significant damage to personal belongings, including beds, furniture, clothing, and toys. Rainfall totals of 5 to 6 inches were reported across the area, leading to flooding of homes and surrounding properties. Above mentioned totals fell within a matter of hours, leading to river overflow and significant Water accumulation. Nearby, the Rio Gurabo USGS river gauge reached flood stage at 16.09 feet at 1:45 PM AST. The information…
properties.epi: An amplifying mid- to upper-level trough, combined with above-normal moisture, maintained an unstable, wet pattern. With previous rain left saturated soils and elevated rivers, heavy rainfall quickly lead to urban flooding, small stream flooding, river flooding, landslides and flash flooding. Significant flooding occurred in Las Piedras, particularly, where several houses where flooded and flash flooded following heavy rainfall.

properties.note: Emergency management reported numerous roads in downtown Smithfield are under 3 to 4 feet of water. Additionally, residences had water entering homes and businesses.
properties.epi: Behind a back door cold front, widespread showers and thunderstorms developed from the late afternoon through the early overnight hours. Numerous reports of flash flooding were reported, along with several damaging wind reports.

properties.note: Heavy rain led to flooding in Willoughby Hills on July 6, 2026. Willoughby Hills Fire Department experienced flooding on the apparatus floor and around the property. There were several instances of road flooding. Impacted roads include State Route 91 and State Route 6, portions of River Road, and Eddy Road near Interstate 271. A stranded motorist had to be removed from their vehicle on Eddy Road near Interstate 271. There were also multiple reports of flooded basements. According to radar estimates, 2 to 4 inches of rain fell in less than three hours with maximum hourly rainfall rates of at…
properties.epi: A frontal boundary settled into the area early on July 5th. Weak low pressure developed along this front and moved into Northwest Ohio the morning of July 5th. This low pressure then remained nearly stationary through the 5th and into the 6th before weakening and exiting to the southeast later on the 6th into the 7th. The front and low pressure combined with a weak trough aloft to encourage periods of showers and thunderstorms from the 5th through the 6th. A warm and very humid airmass combined with weak steering flow to support slow-moving thunderstorms with torrential rainfall rates. There were a few different waves of thunderstorms with heavy rain. An initial batch of thunderstorms tracked across northern Ohio during the morning and early afternoon of the 5th, bringing flash flooding and severe weather to the Youngstown area. An EF-1 tornado and macroburst caused extensive wind…

properties.note: The rain began around 10pm but continued through the night. A swath of 10 to 12 inches of rain fell from near Viburnum to Taum Sauk Mountain to east of Annapolis. A report of 12.25 inches was measured 6 miles northeast of Oates. Flash flooding began around midnight and peaked just before dawn. All creeks and rivers in the area overflowed their banks with water inundating numerous camp sites as well as some homes and roadways. Several residents were forced to evacuate.
properties.epi: A series of thunderstorms tracked across the Missouri Ozarks during the overnight hours of July 9 into July 10. These storms produced very heavy rainfall. A swath of 7 to 12 inches of rain was recorded in about 7 hours leading to widespread flash flooding especially near mountain creeks and streams. The flooding peaked in the early morning hours of July 10, but rescue operations for victims stranded by flooding continued well into the day.

properties.note: Videos from local media and social media showed significant flooding from 1.64 of rain with 3 to 5 feet of water on roadways across Gallup with several vehicles trapped in high water. At least 12 vehicles stranded in several inches of flood waters and mud resulting in water rescues. Numerous roadways were damaged across town. Dozens of buildings and residences have basements full of water. The historic El Rancho Hotel had 4 feet of water in their basement. Flood damage is an estimate.
properties.epi: A plume of monsoon moisture between an upper low over the Permian Basin of western Texas and southeast New Mexico and a disturbance over Arizona resulted in diurnal shower and thunderstorm activity first across the higher terrain before moving south and west into nearby highlands and valley locations. Thunderstorms producing locally heavy rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches resulted in flash flooding in Gallup and Zuni Pueblo during the evening hours of July 16th. Heavy rainfall amounts of up to 2 inches on the South Fork burn scar just west of Ruidoso on July 17th resulted in flash flooding and debris flows on and downstream of the Cedar Creek area. A low water crossing flooded from heavy rains in northwestern Roswell on the 18th, while storms producing flash flooding impacted areas just northeast of Grants, NM on the 19th.

properties.note: The most significant impact occurred south of Orofino, where a large landslide blocked US-12 between mile markers 44 and 45. The initial slide occurred around 1539MST on Friday, March 13. While crews worked to clear the route, a second slide occurred at the same location at 0920MST on Saturday, March 14. The highway remained closed in both directions until Saturday afternoon. Additional landslides and rockslides were reported on Lower Fords Creek Road, Grangemont Road, Sunnyside, and Bobbitt Bench. Heavy traffic diverted to Sunnyside Road caused that secondary route to begin failing under…
properties.epi: An intense and prolonged atmospheric river (AR) impacted the Northern Rockies, directed primarily at North-Central Idaho. This event was characterized by a deep moisture plume and an unseasonably warm air mass, which transitioned mountain snow to a heavy rain-on-snow event. Total precipitation across the Clearwater Basin ranged from 2.5 to over 5.0 inches. Impacts from this storm included power outages and impacts to travel. The biggest impact, however, was flooding in Clearwater County near Orofino. By the morning of March 13, several days of moderate rain and mild temperatures had completely saturated the soil. With the ground unable to absorb any more water and temperatures remaining above freezing overnight, continued rainfall and rapid snowmelt triggered immediate runoff. This surge of water overwhelmed culverts, destabilized hillsides, and caused rapid rises on small streams and…

properties.note: County emergency management reported Delta County Airport closed on the 13th due to water over the runways. Power was cut to the VOR facility and water was at least 3 feet deep. At least 4 roads in the city of Escanaba were closed on the 13th. In Rapid River, water over the road closed the US-41 and US-2 intersection. A culvert washout closed County Road 503 in Bay De Noc Township from the 16th to the 17th. Water over the road on County Road 497/GG in Nahma caused the road to be closed from the 17th to the 27th. Drone footage along the Ford River provided by the emergency manager highlighted…

The flooding also caused damage at the Escanaba Airport (KESC) due to standing water on the runways and power failure. Due to the severity of the flooding, a Disaster Declaration Request was approved by the president on June 30th for Menominee and Marquette counties.

properties.note: Emergency management reported multiple rivers and low lying areas were inundated by the combination of rain and snowmelt. In Gwinn, multiple roadways were inaccessible due to flooding on the Escanaba River by the 18th. Division Street in Negaunee was closed daily from the 13th onwards. Harlow Lake Rd (County Road HD) was closed at County Road 550 on the 17th. Flooding at Pelissier Lake in Sands Township resulted in 1 evacuation with well water being unsafe due to the high water table making septic systems inoperable. Ely, Humboldt, Champion, and Republic townships experienced water over…

properties.note: Several areas experienced flooding in Port Clinton with numerous roads impassable across the city. Impacted and closed roads include Perry Street near Monroe Street, Perry Street at Jefferson Street, East 2nd Street at Beech Street, and State Route 163 near Maple Street. Several residential basements and businesses experienced flooding. Radar estimated 3 to 5 inches of rainfall in less than four hours with maximum rainfall rates of at least 5 to 6 inches per hour during the peak of the heavy rainfall.
