properties.note: Flooding from 2 to 4 inches of heavy rain impacted Muncie neighborhoods, causing property damage that included ruined flooring, flooded homes, and submerged vehicles. Floodwaters also resulted in one woman being hospitalized after a fall inside her home.
properties.epi: On the the late morning of the 11th, a moist and unstable airmass over central Indiana combined with a weak surface boundary to trigger convective development. Steering winds aloft were light, generally moving storms at speeds around 10 mph, which allowed the activity to remain nearly stationary over east-central portions of the state. This environment was highly favorable for efficient precipitation production, resulting in torrential rainfall rates before the storms dissipated in the early afternoon.||Between 11:00 AM and 1:00 PM EST, these slow-moving storms deposited 2 to 4 inches of rain across the Muncie area. The intense rainfall quickly overwhelmed local drainage infrastructure, resulting in significant flooding across multiple residential neighborhoods. Floodwaters completely submerged streets and parked vehicles, while also entering numerous houses. The water intrusion caused…

properties.note: County emergency management reported 20 to 30 roads flooded by 9:45 AM on the 12th, with significant flooding of the US-2 rail underpass in Powers as well as much of the surrounding town and the nearby town of Wilson. On the 13th, railroad tracks in Faithorn were washed out. In the overnight of the 13th into the 14th, County Road 563 washed out at Wilson Creek. One water rescue was performed in Harris Township on the 14th.Due to the severity of the flooding, a Disaster Declaration Request was approved by the president on June 30th.

properties.note: Numerous roads, buildings and vehicles were flooded in and around Blossom, including an RV park, apartment complex, and several homes. Highway 82 through town was flooded and approximately 35 water rescues were reported.
properties.epi: Driven by a weak frontal zone over southern Oklahoma, two separate thunderstorm complexes tracked from west to east over the same areas, causing flash flooding across Lamar County. The bulk of the flooding occurred on June 23 in connection with the second complex. The systems also produced isolated large hail and a single severe wind gust.

properties.note: NY 9J was closed due to flash flooding between Knickerbocker Road and NY Route 150 in the Town of Schodack. Several side streets were also inundated with water including Brickyard Road. A boat and two cars were submerged in water off NY 9J near Brickyard Road.

properties.epi: A strong low-pressure system originating in the Bering Sea moved across mainland Alaska in mid-to-late July 2026, bringing multiple rounds of anomalous, heavy rainfall to Southcentral Alaska that approached record levels for the month. Between July 13 and July 23, persistent wet conditions saturated the region, with the heaviest precipitation focused over the Talkeetna Mountains and the Susitna Valley. The Talkeetna River Basin received 4 to 6 inches of rain, or a 5- to 10-year average recurrence interval. Meanwhile the Yentna Basin saw 10-day totals of 6 to 8 inches. This excessive runoff caused fast-responding rivers and streams to swell, leading to moderate flooding, severe riverbank erosion, road washouts, and a local emergency disaster declaration by the Matanuska-Susitna Borough Assembly.

Damage is an estimate.

properties.epi: A strong upper-level ridge moved over the northern Great Plains allowing a moist, tropical airmass to move over South-Central Texas. Precipitable water values increased to greater than 2.0 inches which were near or above the 95th percentile of climatological values for this part of July. Multiple rounds of excessive rainfall were triggered by mid-level disturbances around the southern periphery of the high and low-level outflow boundaries. This convection was aided by nocturnal low-level jet streaks which led to slow moving, back building thunderstorms. Most of South-Central Texas received more than two inches of rain. The greatest totals were over Uvalde and Kinney Counties where 20-30 inches occurred. Another local maximum of 15-20 inches was observed in central Kerr County. Ten to 15 inches were widespread from Del Rio to Hondo and northward to northeastern Edwards to western…

properties.note: At approximately 800 pm HST, a mesoscale convective system was observed moving over the Kauai Channel towards Oahu. At around 900 pm HST, this mesoscale convective system moved over the west side of Oahu, then the Northern half of Oahu, and began to deliver large amounts of heavy rain. Due to the slow moving nature of this weather system, enormous rain amounts accumulated in a very short time frame. At approximately 1000 pm HST, stream levels rose above flood thresholds and reservoirs filled up. From 1100 pm HST to 200 AM HST, a massive flood wave surged through the North Shore. Multiple…
properties.epi: A cutoff low moved in from the northwest and pulled deep tropical moisture from the south over the Hawaiian islands. This led to the development of prolonged slow moving heavy rain and thunderstorms. The heavy rain and thunderstorms caused catastrophic flooding over Oahu's North Shore and Manoa Valley.

properties.epi: A small sedan attempted to ford Tres Pinos Creek along Browns Valley Road near Paicines on the night of February 17, with first responders responding to the scene during the night. The next morning, the driver was found walking along Highway 25 asking about the location of the passenger. The passenger's body was eventually found a mile downstream of where the car had gotten stranded. The driver was later arrested on charges of gross vehicular manslaughter. At the time of the incident, the TESC1 river gauge on Tres Pinos Creek measured stages above 2 feet, compared to a typical stage of less than a foot. While conditions did not meet WWA Criteria, the threat of heavy rain and flooding was messages by the WFO ahead of the event.

properties.note: Heavy rainfall generated flash flooding from Maria Ygnacio Creek. One man was swept down the creek and drowned. His body was found in the creek near the intersection of San Marcos Road and Via Parva.
properties.epi: A powerful winter storm brought heavy rain to Southwestern California. Widespread rainfall totals between 2 and 5 inches were reported. With the heavy rain, there were numerous reports of flash flooding and mud/debris flows.

properties.note: One person was swept away by flood waters one mile west of Raccoon Road at Shoal Creek in Newton county.
properties.epi: Severe thunderstorms with tornadoes and damaging winds occurred late in the evening of June 13, 2026. Repeated rounds of heavy rainfall caused flash flooding and river flooding. Between 3 and 6 inches of rainfall fell with this system. Some fatalities occurred from the flooding.

properties.note: Lingering floodwaters remained after heavy rainfall, along with some reports of wrecks and high water in spots. The most significant report came from local broadcast news station. They reported that first responders received a call around 6pm that a 15 year old had gone missing after walking into floodwaters near a retention pond near Turriff Circle just west of The Woodlands. The 15 year old did not resurface. Boats and dive teams attempted to complete a rescue and discovered that the 15 year old had drowned.
properties.epi: Multiple rounds of flash flooding occurred throughout Southeast Texas over the course of several days, leading up to Tropical storm Arthur.

properties.note: A teenage girl drowned after being trapped under debris in fast flowing water.
properties.epi: High water on the Licking River resulted in a fatality.

properties.note: The body of a man was recovered in the Stillwater River after the man entered the Englewood Recreational Reservoir water and did not resurface.
properties.epi: A fatality occurred when a man entered the Englewood Recreational Reservoir water and did not resurface.

properties.note: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. A vehicle was swept away at the 1500 block of Lower Mason Creek Rd. into Mason Creek. One person was found dead in the vehicle approximately two miles downstream.
properties.epi: A cold front moved into South-Central Texas and stalled. The airmass the front moved into was warm and very moist. Thunderstorms formed in the vicinity of the front and some of these storms produced locally heavy rain that led to flash flooding.

properties.note: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding sending San Pedro Creek out of its banks near Furnish Ave. and S. San Marcos St. San Antonio firefighters were called to the scene to execute a high-water rescue. They recovered a man, but he was pronounced dead at the scene. Police stated a jogger or walker was pulled into the creek by the high water.
properties.epi: Thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a stationary front, and some of these storms produced large hail and damaging wind gusts.

properties.note: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain Monday and Monday night across the northeast side of San Antonio. Between 4 and 6 inches of rain occurred. This caused a quick rise into flood stage on Salado Creek early Tuesday morning. A 44 year old man was killed by the flood waters in the Salado Creek Greenway, near J Street Park. Authorities were not able to determine how the man got into the water, but was suspected of being homeless and living near the creek.
properties.epi: Persistent isentropic lift generated showers and thunderstorms that led to excessive rainfall and flash flooding.

properties.note: Three people went swimming in the swollen Floyds Fork at Broad Run Park when one of them, a man in his 20s, got pulled under by the current. Given recent rains the river was elevated, but still within its banks. The Mt Washington, Floyds Fork, gauge was around 12.5 feet at the time.
properties.epi: Multiple rounds of storms occurred June 26-28th, 2026 resulting in significant flash flooding over southern Indiana and central Kentucky as well as an EF-0 tornado. Several flash flood warnings were issued over the 2 day period with Considerable Flash Flooding in multiple locations and even Flash Flood Emergencies in some areas. Rainfall totals for the weekend ended up in an area wide 2-4 inches with swaths of 6-10+ inches!! Unfortunately 3 fatalities were confirmed due to flooding in Madison County, KY, and 1 fatality indirectly related to the flooding occurred on Floyds Fork in Jefferson County, KY.

properties.note: Swift water rescue on Julian Wash at Palo Verde Rd. One person deceased.
properties.epi: Active monsoon period continues with flash flooding across the Tucson Metro that led to multiple road closures and a death in the Julian Wash due to flooding.

properties.note: A car was swept off Tates Creek Road into a stream which was well out of its banks.

properties.epi: A mid-level shortwave trough moved around the south side of a ridge across South-Central Texas and interacted with a warm, moist airmass. This disturbance generated thunderstorms that produced locally heavy rain leading to flash flooding.

properties.note: Significant rainfall farther upstream within the Howard Draw watershed led to rapid riverine flooding along Howard Draw and downstream along the Pecos River in western Val Verde County. The Pecos River gauge at Pandale Crossing just downstream of the Howard Draw confluence registered a steep and significant rise on the evening of July 17, rising to a crest of 15.93ft (89,700cfs) in Major flood at 2115CST. properties.note: The Uvalde area and Leona River watershed received some of the heaviest rainfall in South-Central Texas during the July 2026 flood event. Rounds of torrential rain occurred each morning between July 14 and July 16. The headwaters of the Leona River saw 20 to 30 inches of rain during a 3-day stretch. CoCoRaHS observers reported 10 to 15 inches in the Uvalde area. ||Uvalde was among the areas most impacted by the flooding. Some homes experienced 3ft of inundation. A 65 year old man was killed when the house he was in was swept into the Guadalupe River near Goat Creek Rd. in Kerrville. His body was recovered several miles downstream in the 300 block of Center Point River Rd.

properties.note: Two workers inside an underground sewer system became trapped by rising waters and were swept away inside of the sewer system. They were originally working in the 800 block of Curtiss Street. One of the workers was located a few hours later about 200 feet from the original point of entry and was taken to a hospital in good condition. The second worker was recovered the next day and pronounced dead at the scene.
properties.epi: Multiple supercell thunderstorms moved from north to south across northeast Illinois from the late morning through the early evening of July 27th. Widespread and extensive wind damage occurred in many areas. Large hail occurred in many areas. A total of seven tornadoes occurred. Flooding was reported in numerous areas. At the peak of the storms, at least 500,000 customers were without power in northeast Illinois.

properties.note: Swift water rescue reported for two individuals in the Santa Cruz River, with one fatality and two injuries. MRMS Multi-Sensor estimated between 1.0-1.5 inches of rainfall fell in multiple locations nearby.
properties.epi: Strong to severe thunderstorms moved northward through Southeastern Arizona the afternoon and evening of June 17th, 2026. These storms caused thunderstorm wind damage causing 8 power poles to be downed and 7,000 customers to be without power in the Tucson Metro and damage to a power transformer that caused a power outage for Tohono O'odham Nation. Heavy rainfall from thunderstorms caused flash flooding in normally dry rivers and washes that resulted in multiple swift water rescues that resulted in 1 fatality and 2 injuries. Additionally, multiple roadways in Cochise County was impassible due to flooding. An estimated penny sized hail was reported on the SW side of Tucson.

properties.note: The East Fork White River, rising amid moderate flood stage at Shoals, inundated Sprout Springs Road, which swept an elderly man's truck off the road on the 9th, and while the vehicle's passenger was later rescued from a tree vine, search efforts continued for the man through following days.
properties.epi: During March 3 to March 7, 2026, large surface high pressure from the southeastern United States into the Atlantic focused a broad fetch of Gulf moisture northward into the Midwest. A quasi-stationary frontal boundary near the Ohio Valley provided lift and focused, at times heavy rainfall over much of central Indiana, especially along the valley of the East Fork White River, and its tributaries northeast of Columbus through east-central central Indiana.||From the morning of the 3rd through dawn on the 4th, heavy rainfall over the watershed of the East Fork White's headwaters totaled mainly 2.00-3.75 inches. Additional 1-day rainfall to dawn on the 5th, along the river's main stem from Columbus down through Martin County totaled generally 1.50-3.00 inches. Further 2.5-day rainfall through late on the 7th was generally 1.00-2.00 inches along this main stem. Overall 4.5-day rainfall…

properties.note: A partially submerged vehicle was found in the North Branch Callicoon Creek at around 7 AM EDT on July 29th. Further investigation indicated that the vehicle was traveling northbound along a road parallel to the creek and struck a telephone pole before crashing into the creek. The deceased driver was located several hours later approximately 2.5 miles downstream. Specific cause of death is unknown at this time, however, widespread flooding was ongoing on Callicoon Creek and tributaries.
properties.epi: An area of low pressure slowly moving across the region, along with an associated frontal boundary and supporting upper energy, brought multiple rounds of showers and embedded strong thunderstorms with locally heavy rainfall. The slow-moving nature of the convection combined with strong mid level winds, also known as a low level jet, enhancing moisture and lift, especially over the Catskills, resulted in rainfall totals of 3 to 6 inches and widespread flash flooding across Sullivan County.

properties.note: A vehicle was swept off a low water bridge on State Highway CC due to flash flooding. One of the occupants was able to self rescue however the other occupant was found deceased in the vehicle.

properties.note: River flooding in northeastern Jackson County was exasperated locally by heavy rainfall during the overnight of the 4th-5th around 2.00 inches, with the East Fork White River later cresting at Seymour in major flood stage on the 5th evening. On the 6th morning around 700EST, a man in an airboat near Courtland, while attempting to rescue individuals stranded in a submerged vehicle, died after the boat experienced mechanical issues, capsized, and was swept under a bridge.

properties.note: Rain began around 10PM on the evening of July 9, but storms increased in intensity and persistence shortly after midnight. By morning, a swath of 7 to 10 inches of rain had fallen across southern Crawford County from near Cedar Ford to near Viburnum. This led to flash flooding along every creek and river in the area, with much of this water flowing through the Huzzah Creek. Camp sites along the river were inundated as well as homes and roadways. Numerous water rescues and evacuations were required. One person was killed in floodwaters after her home was swept off its foundation with her…
properties.epi: A series of thunderstorms tracked across the Missouri Ozarks during the overnight hours of July 9 into July 10. These storms produced very heavy rainfall. A swath of 7 to 12 inches of rain was recorded in about 7 hours leading to widespread flash flooding especially near mountain creeks and streams. The flooding peaked in the early morning hours of July 10, but rescue operations for victims stranded by flooding continued well into the day.

properties.note: Two people were trapped and drowned in a basement apartment on the 300 block of University Drive after the outside entrance, 10 feet below ground level, filled with water.

properties.epi: Continuing an active monsoon period with heavy rainfall caused running washes and rivers that led to impassable roadways. Additionally, there was 2 deaths in the Santa Cuz river due to drowning.

properties.note: The East Fork White River, while cresting in moderate flood stage in southeastern Lawrence County, swept away a truck carrying two people during the overnight early on the 9th. Both occupants were found submerged in 8 feet of water west of the Tunnelton community near the intersection of Earl Road and Lawrenceport Road.

properties.note: Stonecoal Lake Road began to flood and stranded a vehicle. At 630 PM EST, two people drowned after their vehicle was swept away by flash flooding from the Right Fork of Stonecoal Creek while traveling along County Route 7. Time is an estimate provided by law enforcement. Around 7 PM EST, floodwaters also trapped a person on top of a camper along Stonecoal Lake Road.
properties.epi: An upper level trough descended into the northeast quadrant of the United States while a surface low ambled east across Ontario and Quebec. The system first lifted a warm front through the middle Ohio Valley and Central Appalachians on the night of July 20th into the early morning of the 21st, then steered a cold front east across the area late that evening into the night.||Showers and thunderstorms began to develop by late morning on the 21st, with a broken line of stronger storms progressing across the area during the afternoon and evening. Severe thunderstorms produced two main swaths of damage across the area. The first swath of damage encompassed areas along and north of a line from Wood County east to Randolph County, while the second was primarily concentrated along and near the I-64 corridor. In addition to numerous reports of downed trees and power outages, some notable areas…

properties.note: Heavy rainfall that occurred during the morning of June 14th caused the James River at Springfield to reach moderate flood stage. This caused elevated stream flows at Lake Springfield. Four individuals went into Lake Springfield during the afternoon of June 14th and went over the Springfield Lake Dam where their devices were capsized. Three individuals drowned in the incident and the other had moderate injuries. A Flood Warning was in effect at the time of the incident.

properties.note: Video shared from broadcast media of a flash flood wave and debris out of Sunglow canyon crossing the road near Bicknell. Subsequently, the Wayne County Sheriff reported 5 deceased in a wash near Sunglow Campground, believed to have fallen victim to flooding from heavy rainfall.
properties.epi: A monsoonal pattern persisted onward through mid July, resulting in more instances of thunderstorm winds and flash flooding.
